quantity: Largest N with Robin's inequality σ(n) < e^γ n log log n verified for every 5040 < n ≤ N
statement: Robin's inequality holds for every integer n with 5040 < n ≤ 10^(10^13.11485). Equivalently (Corollary 14, restated as Axler 2023 Lemma 2.3), it holds for every n with 5041 ≤ n ≤ N_{k0}, where k0 = 999,999,476,056 and p_{k0} = 29,996,208,012,611. The proof checks consecutive colossally abundant (CA) numbers with Briggs's algorithm in 100-bit interval arithmetic. By Robin's lemma, checking the CA numbers covers every integer between them. The last CA number checked is listed explicitly in the proof.
location: Theorem 13 and Corollary 14, §4 'Computations', p. 6 of arXiv v4 (20 Jul 2020)

history.note: Robin checked CA numbers C with P(C) < 20000. The range is as reconstructed in Caveney–Nicolas–Sondow 2012, proof of Thm 5 (fulltext).
Computation over CA numbers; source is the zbMATH review.
100-bit interval arithmetic. The improvement is ×1300 in log10 log10 N.

caveats: (1) This is a finite verification. By Robin, if RH fails then counterexamples exist, but nothing bounds where the first one lies, so the range carries no global information. Johnston–Trudgian (arXiv 2511.09978, to appear in Anal. Math.) quantify the same locality barrier for M(x). (2) As far as I found, no independent replication exists. The authors thank Briggs for sharing his code. The arXiv text points to no public artifact or hash. (3) The arXiv text does not say whether Briggs's 2006 run used directed rounding. MP re-ran it with interval arithmetic. (4) The record still stood in Oct 2026: Leshchiner–Musin–Thompson (arXiv 2610.39120) cite MP as the current range. (5) Lagarias's inequality holds over the same range by an elementary implication; see ARITH-LAGARIAS.

source.title: Robin's inequality for 20-free integers

verification.checked_against: arXiv 1809.10813v4 full text (Thm 13, Cor 14, §5, acknowledgements); Axler arXiv 2110.13478v3 Lemma 2.3; zbMATH 7342413 (Integers 21 (2021) A28); Leshchiner–Musin–Thompson arXiv 2610.39120v1 intro; web and arXiv search for any extension in 2025–2026 (none found).
verification.correction: (a) The step from Briggs's 10^(10^10) to 10^(10^13.11485) multiplies log10 N (equivalently log N) by 10^3.11485 ≈ 1303. It adds 3.11 to log10 log10 N; it does not multiply that quantity by 1300. The frontier's historical_improvement repeats the slip. (b) MP Corollary 14 is stated as 'for all 13# ≤ n ≤ 29 996 208 012 611#', not for 5041 ≤ n. Axler's Lemma 2.3 (5041 ≤ n ≤ N_k0) is described by Axler as 'a slightly better result' implied by MP's argument, so it is not merely a restatement. N_k0 = p_k0# slightly exceeds 10^(10^13.11485): log N_k0 = θ(p_k0) ≈ 2.99962·10^13 versus 2.9996162·10^13.
verification.notes: Theorem 13, 100-bit interval arithmetic, the explicit last CA number checked and the acknowledgement of Briggs's code are all confirmed verbatim. No public artifact or hash is cited. No newer range was found; LMT (Oct 2026) still cite MP. The 1984 value e^19747 ≈ 10^8576 is arithmetically consistent.

quantity: Largest t such that Robin's inequality is proved for all t-free n > 5040
statement: Robin's inequality holds for every 21-free integer n ≥ 5041. Hence RH holds if and only if Robin's inequality holds for every 21-full integer. A second, independent proof (ACP Theorem 2.16) uses the Axler–Nicolas bound n/φ(n) < e^γ log log n + 0.0168/(log log n)^2 for n ≥ 10^(10^13.11485), together with the Morrill–Platt range.
location: Theorem 1.2 and Corollary 2.5 (proof §2, pp. 2–4 of arXiv v3). Independent proof: Assani–Chester–Paschal, Theorem 2.16 (arXiv 2503.03159v2 §2.4; Integers 26 (2026) A86).

history.note: J. Théor. Nombres Bordeaux 19 (2007) 357–372 (zbMATH pages; arXiv journal-ref gives 351–366)
Uses Dusart 2018 product bound; see erratum chain

caveats: (1) Morrill–Platt (§5) state that their own method fails at t = 21, since g_B(29 996 208 012 611; 21) > 1 and g_∞(B; 21) > 1. Axler gets past this with sharper explicit Mertens-product and θ bounds. (2) arXiv v3 of Axler cites these bounds as '[3] C. Axler, Effective estimates for some functions defined over primes, in progress'. That paper later appeared in Integers 24 (2024) A34 (zbMATH 7852320). I did not check that the published propositions match the versions used. (3) The 20-free proof of MP takes its product bound (MP Thm 11, valid for x ≥ 767,135,587) from Dusart 2018, p. 245. Broadbent–Fiori–Kadiri–Ng–Wilk (arXiv 2608.01498) state that the proofs of all of Dusart 2018's Mertens-sum and Mertens-product corollaries are invalid and that they recover them; see ARITH-MERTENS-PRODUCT-EXPLICIT. The 21-free results do not appear to use those corollaries. (4) Heuristic, my own unpublished estimate from a float computation up to 10^8 (script arith_scripts/mertens_product.py): the method needs e^{-γ}∏_{p≤x}p/(p−1)/log θ(x) − 1 below roughly 2^{-t} for all x ≥ p_{k0}. The true excess appears to be about (0.3–1.1)/(√x log x), so even with perfect information the method stalls near t ≈ log2(√p_max log p_max) ≈ 27 at the current range. Each further unit of t needs about 4× larger p_max. The t-free route therefore cannot reach all integers.

source.title: On Robin's inequality

verification.checked_against: Axler arXiv 2110.13478v3 (Thm 1.2, Lemmas 2.1–2.4, Cor 2.5, refs [3], [7]); ACP arXiv 2503.03159v2 §2.4 (eq. (36), Thm 2.15–2.16); zbMATH 7713337, 7852320 (Axler, Integers 24 (2024) A34), 8227947 (ACP, Integers 26 (2026) A86); MP §5; the drafter's script arith_scripts/mertens_product.py; Nicolas arXiv 1202.0729 Thm 1.1.
verification.correction: The record (t = 21) and its sources are correct. Caveat (4) is numerically wrong. The drafter's script computes e^{-γ}∏_{p≤x}p/(p−1)/log x − 1, using log x where the stated quantity, and the t-free criterion (Axler Lemma 2.4), use log θ(x). With the correct normalisation the excess at x = p_k is e^{-γ}c(N_k)/(√θ log θ), where c(N_k) ∈ [2.2086, 4.0628] under RH (Nicolas 2012 (1.6)–(1.7), checked numerically to p_k ≤ 10^9). That is ≈ (1.24–2.28)/(√x log x), or about 0.7–1.3·10^{-8} at p_k0. It is not (0.3–1.1)/(√x log x) ≈ 2–7·10^{-9}. With perfect information the heuristic ceiling is therefore t ≈ 26, not 27. The '4× p_max per unit of t' scaling is correct.
verification.notes: Axler's Theorem 1.4 (ν2(n) ≤ 20 ⇒ Robin) already implies the 21-free theorem. ACP's proof is likewise a ν2-based argument using the Axler–Nicolas bound (Acta Arith. 209 (2022)) plus the MP range, so 'independent' means only that it uses a different input bound. Axler's proof uses '[3] in progress', later Integers 24 (2024) A34. I did not check that its Prop. 1.1 and 3.4 survived publication unchanged.

quantity: Structural constraints on the least counterexample c > 5040 to Robin's inequality, if one exists
statement: If c is the least integer > 5040 that violates Robin's inequality, then: (a) c is superabundant (Akbary–Friggstad 2009) and extremely abundant (Nazardonyavi–Yakubovich, Thm 2.3). (b) c is even and neither squarefree nor squarefull (CLMS 2007), and c is not 21-free (Axler 2023). (c) ν2(c) ≥ 21, ν5(c) ≥ 9, ν_p(c) ≥ 5 for 11 < p ≤ 19, ≥ 4 for 19 < p ≤ 41, ≥ 3 for 41 < p ≤ 139, and ≥ 2 for 139 < p ≤ 1777 (Axler 2023 Thm 1.4). Also ν3(c) ≥ 13, ν7(c) ≥ 7, ν11(c) ≥ 6 (Hertlein 2018 Thm 2, as restated by Axler). (d) c > 10^(10^13.11485) (Morrill–Platt). (e) If RH is false, then μ := max_{n>5040} G(n) exists, with G(n) = σ(n)/(n log log n). Every maximiser is both GA2 and CA (CNS 2012 Thm 5(iii)), and the least maximiser is 'extraordinary' (CNS 2011). RH holds iff 4 is the only extraordinary number. A GA2 number > 5040 exists iff RH is false. (f) Unrefereed: ω(c) ≥ 969,672,728, fewer than ω(c)/14 exponents of c exceed 1, and e^{-log p1}ω(c) < p_{ω(c)}/log c < 1 (Vojak, Thm 1.6). RH holds iff there are infinitely many extremely abundant numbers (N–Y Thm 2.4).
value: c superabundant ∩ extremely abundant, 21-full, ν2 ≥ 21, c > 10^(10^13.11485); ω(c) ≥ 969,672,728 (preprint)
location: N–Y arXiv 1211.2147 Thm 2.3–2.4 (p. 4); CNS arXiv 1112.6010 Thm 4, Thm 5(ii)–(iii), Cor. 1 (pp. 4, 13–15); Axler Thm 1.4 (p. 2); Vojak Thm 1.6 (p. 4); CLMS abstract/zbMATH 5302779; Akbary–Friggstad via the zbMATH summary and N–Y ref. [1]

history.value: even, not squarefree/squarefull, divisible by a 5th power
RH ⟺ 4 is the only extraordinary number; GA2 > 5040 exists ⟺ RH false

caveats: (1) CLMS arXiv v2 comment: 'In the first version in Theorem 5 (main result) it was falsely asserted that n must be superabundant, invalidating the proof'. The published version uses a different proof. (2) CNS Cor. 1 ('no GA2 number between 5041 and 10^8576') rests on Robin's 1984 range. Each GA2 number has G(N) ≥ e^γ (CNS eq. (3)), so with Morrill–Platt's range the same argument gives that any GA2 number > 5040 exceeds 10^(10^13.11485). This is my rigorous inference, not a published statement. (3) Vojak is an unrefereed arXiv preprint (zbMATH lists it as a preprint), and his ω-bound uses Briggs's 10^(10^10). Putting the MP range into his argument, log p_{ω(c)} > (L + √(L² − 4))/2 with L = log log c > 31.03, would give ω(c) of order 10^12. That is my unpublished arithmetic and is not certified. (4) Akbary–Friggstad's evidence is the zbMATH summary plus the citation in N–Y. I did not read the full text.

source.authors: A. Akbary, Z. Friggstad; Y.-J. Choie, N. Lichiardopol, P. Moree, P. Solé; S. Nazardonyavi, S. Yakubovich; G. Caveney, J.-L. Nicolas, J. Sondow; C. Axler; R. Vojak
source.title: Superabundant numbers and the RH (Amer. Math. Monthly 116 (2009) 273–275); On Robin's criterion for the RH (JTNB 2007); Extremely abundant numbers and the RH (J. Integer Seq. 17 (2014) 14.2.8); On SA, CA, and GA numbers (Ramanujan J. 29 (2012)); On Robin's inequality (2023); On numbers satisfying Robin's inequality… (arXiv 2005.09307, 2020)

verification.checked_against: Axler 2110.13478v3 Thm 1.4 and the Hertlein restatement (ν2≤19, ν3≤12, ν5≤7, ν7≤6, ν11≤5); CNS arXiv 1112.6010 (abstract and Thm 4; GA2 > 5040 ⟺ RH false, then N > 10^8576); N–Y arXiv 1211.2147 Thms 2.3–2.4; Vojak arXiv 2005.09307 Thm 1.6 (ω(c) ≥ 969 672 728, using Briggs's c > 10^10^10); CLMS abstract (math/0604314); ACP refs for Akbary–Friggstad (AMM 116 (2009) 273–275).
verification.notes: All the listed valuations and structural claims match the sources. Akbary–Friggstad is still secondary only. Two relevant structural results are absent (see missing_records). Wu (arXiv 1903.03490, Cor. 4, as restated by Leshchiner–Musin–Thompson 2026) shows RH ⟺ G(n) < e^γ for every CA2 number n > 5040, so a least CA counterexample can be sought in CA2. Luca–Solé (Integers 25 (2025) A8, with a later Luca–Pomerance–Solé corrigendum) give #{5040 < n ≤ x : Robin fails} ≪ x^ε. The extrapolation of Vojak's ω-bound to the MP range (ω(c) ~ 10^12) is plausible: a superabundant c has p_ω(c) ≈ log c ≈ 3·10^13. It remains the drafter's own uncertified arithmetic.

quantity: Best unconditional multiplicative constant ε in σ(n)/n < (1+ε) e^γ log log n for all n outside a finite explicit exceptional set
statement: For every positive integer n outside the set A ∪ {3, 720}, σ(n)/n < (1 + 3.15367·10^{-7}) e^γ log log n. Here A = {1, 2, 4, 5, 6, 8, 9, 10, 12, 16, 18, 20, 24, 30, 36, 48, 60, 72, 84, 120, 180, 240, 360, 840, 2520, 5040}, the 26 known exceptions to Robin's inequality. The proof comes from Theorem 1.3: σ(n)/n < e^γ log log n (1 + 0.0094243/(log log n)^3) for n ∉ A, combined with the Morrill–Platt range.
location: Theorem 1.3 (p. 2) and Corollary 3.1 (§3, p. 4) of arXiv v3

history.value: σ(n)/n ≤ e^γ log log n + 0.6483/log log n (n ≥ 3)
history.note: Additive form, as quoted in Axler (1.5)
Hertlein Thm 4, as quoted by Axler

caveats: The constant is set entirely by the verified range: 0.0094243/(log p_{k0})^3 = 3.1537·10^{-7}, using log log N_{k0} ≈ log p_{k0} ≈ 31.03; I recomputed this. Any extension of the certified Robin range therefore improves ε directly. Pushing ε below 0 for all large n is exactly RH. The unconditional bound depends on Axler's 2024 explicit estimates; see the dependency caveat in ARITH-ROBIN-TFREE.

source.title: On Robin's inequality

verification.checked_against: Axler 2110.13478v3 Thm 1.3, Cor 3.1 and its proof, eq. (1.5) and the Hertlein quotation; my own exact computation of every n < 6000 violating Robin, Thm 1.3 and Cor 3.1.
verification.correction: (a) A is not 'the 26 known exceptions to Robin's inequality'. The integers 3 ≤ n ≤ 5040 violating Robin are 3, 4, 5, 6, 8, 9, 10, 12, 16, 18, 20, 24, 30, 36, 48, 60, 72, 84, 120, 180, 240, 360, 720, 840, 2520, 5040 (26 numbers; 27 with n = 2). Axler's A is {1, 2} ∪ (that list minus {3, 720}), i.e. the exceptional set of Theorem 1.3. A ∪ {3, 720} = {1, 2} ∪ the Robin exceptions. I verified by computation that 3 and 720 violate Cor 3.1 but satisfy Thm 1.3. (b) The 1984 history note 'Additive form, as quoted in Axler (1.5)' is wrong. Axler's (1.5) is the multiplicative form e^γ log log n (1 + 0.6483/(log log n)^2), which is weaker by a factor e^γ in the correction term. Robin's original additive constant is (σ(12)/12 − e^γ log log 12) log log 12 = 0.648213…, which I recomputed.
verification.notes: ε = 3.15367·10^{-7} = 0.0094243/(31.032)^3 is confirmed. Axler's proof requires log log n ≥ (a0/ε)^{1/3} = 31.0321 ≤ log θ(p_k0). Hertlein's 5.645·10^{-7} is confirmed as quoted by Axler.

quantity: Lagarias harmonic-number criterion: status and verified range
statement: RH is equivalent to σ(n) ≤ H_n + exp(H_n) log H_n for all n ≥ 1, with equality only for n = 1 (Lagarias 2002). Since H_n > log n + γ, exp(H_n) log H_n > e^γ n log log n for n ≥ 3, so Robin's inequality at n implies Lagarias's at n. Lagarias's inequality therefore holds for 5041 ≤ n ≤ 10^(10^13.11485) by Morrill–Platt Theorem 13; Lagarias treated n ≤ 5040 directly. If counterexamples exist, the least one is superabundant: B_n = (H_n + e^{H_n} log H_n)/n is strictly increasing (MacArevey 2026, preprint). The Kaneko–Lagarias variant also reduces to superabundant numbers (Assani–Chester–Paschal, Thm 3.9).
value: verified for n ≤ 10^(10^13.11485) (inherited from Robin range)
location: Main theorem (zbMATH 1956329 review). Superabundant reduction: MacArevey arXiv 2602.15905 (abstract). Kaneko–Lagarias: ACP Thm 3.9 (arXiv 2503.03159v2 §3).
caveats: The implication Robin ⇒ Lagarias for n ≥ 3 uses only H_n > log n + γ. I state it here as an elementary inference, not a quotation. I did not re-read Lagarias's proof for n ≤ 5040. MacArevey (Feb 2026) is unrefereed and I read only its abstract. AI-assisted 'verified finite Lagarias certificates' (arXiv 2606.15096) cover only finite ranges and carry no global content.

source.title: An elementary problem equivalent to the Riemann hypothesis

verification.checked_against: ACP 2503.03159v2 Thm 3.9 and Thm 3.10 (Robin at n ⇒ Kaneko–Lagarias at n); MacArevey arXiv 2602.15905 abstract (v2); arXiv 2606.15096 abstract; ACP ref [11] for the Lagarias bibliographic data; my own check of the Robin ⇒ Lagarias implication.
verification.notes: I checked the implication: H_n > log n + γ gives e^{H_n} > e^γ n and log H_n > log log n, so for n ≥ 3, σ(n) < e^γ n log log n < e^{H_n} log H_n. The inherited range is valid. Lagarias's main theorem itself was not re-read in full text. MacArevey is unrefereed and only its abstract was read. The 2606.15096 AI 'finite certificates' carry no global content, as the draft says.

quantity: Nicolas φ-criterion at primorials N_k and the normalized defect c(n) = (n/φ(n) − e^γ log log n)√(log n)
statement: RH holds iff N_k/φ(N_k) > e^γ log log N_k for every k ≥ 1 (Nicolas 1983). If RH fails, the inequality holds for infinitely many k and fails for infinitely many k. Under RH (Nicolas 2012, Thm 1.1): limsup c(n) = e^γ(2+β) = 3.6444150964…, where β = 2 + γ − log 4π = 0.0461914179…; c(n) < e^γ(2+β) for n ≥ N_{120569}; c(n) ≤ c(N_66) = 4.0628356921… for n ≥ 2; and c(N_k) ≥ c(2) = 2.2085892614… for k ≥ 1. Each of these four assertions is equivalent to RH (Cor. 1.1). If RH fails, liminf c(n) = −∞ and limsup c(n) = +∞.
value: limsup c(n) = 3.6444150964… (under RH); c(N_k) computed for p_k ≤ 10^9
conditional_on: RH for the explicit constants. The equivalences in Cor. 1.1 are unconditional.
location: Theorem 1.1 and Corollary 1.1 (pp. 2–3); computation in §4 (p. 13). Original criterion: Nicolas, J. Number Theory 17 (1983) 375–388.

history.value: sharp RH-conditional constants; numerical check p_k ≤ 10^9 (30-digit floats)

caveats: (1) For k ≤ 50,847,534 (p_k ≤ 10^9), c(N_k) was 'calculated in Maple with 30 decimal digits, so that we may think that the first ten are correct'. This is ordinary floating point, not certified, so the finite Nicolas check is a non-rigorous computation. (2) Choie–Planat–Solé (arXiv 1012.3613) show that proving the criterion through strict monotonicity of the natural sequence would contradict Cramér's conjecture. This is a negative result conditional on Cramér. (3) I found no published certified range for the Nicolas inequality beyond 10^9. A certified extension via Büthe-type θ bounds up to 10^19 looks feasible but is not in print as far as I found.

verification.checked_against: Nicolas arXiv 1202.0729v2: Thm 1.1 (1.4)–(1.7), Cor 1.1, §3 computation ('Maple with 30 decimal digits … first ten are correct', k0 = 50 847 534, k1 = 120 568); zbMATH 6090471 (Acta Arith. 155 (2012) 311–321); Choie–Planat–Solé arXiv 1012.3613 abstract.
verification.notes: All constants match, and I recomputed β and e^γ(2+β) = 3.6444150964. The 10^9 computation is part of a conditional proof, not a certified verification of Nicolas's inequality. A web search found no certified range beyond it. The RH-conditional analogue for σ(n) (Nicolas, Ramanujan J. 58 (2022) 1113–1157) is missing from the ledger.

quantity: Largest X with |M(x)| < √x verified for all 1 < x ≤ X (exhaustive)
statement: M(n) was computed for every n ≤ 10^16 by a segmented sieve with exact integer arithmetic, recording all extrema, all 366,567,325 zeros, and values at multiples of 10^8. The largest |M(n)| in this range are −35,629,003 and 40,371,499. The extreme ratios q(n) = M(n)/√n reported for the large-n range are −0.525 and 0.571 (q(7,766,842,813) = 0.571). Hence |M(x)| < √x for all 1 < x ≤ 10^16. Over all n ≥ 2 the maximum of |q| is 0.894, at n = 5.
value: X = 10^16 (sup over large n of |q| = 0.571)
location: §6.1–6.2 (pp. 8–9 of arXiv v2) with extrema table; validation described in §6.1

history.note: No extension of the exhaustive range since then

caveats: (1) Johnston–Trudgian (arXiv 2511.09978v4, eq. (34)) quote this as '|M(x)| ≤ 0.571√x for 2 ≤ x ≤ 10^16'. That is false for small x: M(5) = −2 gives 0.894, and M(32) = −4 gives 0.707. My exact integer recomputation (script arith_scripts/mertens_small.py) shows the 0.571 bound holds for 33 ≤ n ≤ 10^7 and fails last at n = 32. The slip does not affect their conclusions. (2) No third party has replicated the full range. Hurst's 2026 preprint (arXiv 2607.07566) re-ran the sieve to 10^16 in 7.39 days, but it descends from the same implementation. (3) Isolated values extend far beyond the exhaustive range but certify nothing about the intervals between them: M(10^23) = 62,467,771,689 (Helfgott–Thompson), and M(10^24) = 7,189,337,839 and M(10^25) = −258,560,632,948 (Hurst 2026, unrefereed). (4) Locality: Johnston–Trudgian show that |M(x)| ≤ 0.571√x up to 10^16 implies only that there are no simple zeros with β > 0.99 and γ < 5.

source.title: Computations of the Mertens function and improved bounds on the Mertens conjecture

verification.checked_against: Hurst arXiv 1610.08551v2 §1, §6.1 (extrema table, 366 567 325 zeros, validation against Deléglise–Rivat values), §6.2; zbMATH 6825256; Hurst arXiv 2607.07566v1 §1–2 and §8.3 (history; 7.39-day re-run; descended implementation; M(10^24), M(10^25)); Johnston–Trudgian 2511.09978v4 eq. quantity: Best proven bounds limsup M(x)/√x ≥ L+ and liminf M(x)/√x ≤ −L−
statement: limsup_{x→∞} M(x)/√x > 1.826054 and liminf_{x→∞} M(x)/√x < −1.837625. The proof uses Ingham's theorem, liminf q ≤ h(y,N) ≤ limsup q with h(y,N) = 2Σ_{i≤N} a_i f(γ_i/γ_N) cos(γ_i y + ψ_i), a_i = 1/|ρ_i ζ'(ρ_i)|, and f(t) = (1−t)cos πt + sin(πt)/π. Values y± ≈ 1.50546·10^5096 and −2.58842·10^5097 were found by LLL (fplll) with ν = 17,000 and N = 800, and h(y±, 14400) was evaluated. The statement is unconditional: if RH fails or some zero is multiple, then q is unbounded.
location: Theorem 6.1, §6.3 (p. 11 of arXiv v2); Ingham's theorem as Thm 4.2 (p. 5); outlook §7.3 (p. 14)

history.note: Ingham/Anderson–Stark route: no relation Σc_iγ_i = 0 among 500 zeros with |c_i| ≤ 4976. The arXiv journal-ref wrongly gives pp. 2433–2446, which are Saouter–Trudgian–Demichel's pages.

caveats: (1) Rigor label. The result is stated as a theorem in a refereed paper. The arXiv text, however, describes 10,000-digit zeros and ~8151-digit ζ'(ρ) computed in Mathematica and 'verified using PARI/GP'. It documents no interval or directed-rounding enclosure for h(y±, 14400), and the values are reported with '≈'. Under this archive's rule that ordinary high precision is not certification, I label it a non-rigorous (uncertified high-precision) computation. The margin over the previous record (1.6383) is very large, so an error is implausible, but not certified. (2) Kim–Nguyen 2025 use Hurst's zero data inside Arb for other kernels, which does not certify Theorem 6.1. (3) Hurst estimates that ±2.00 needs N ≈ 1125 and about 10 months with LLL, and that going beyond 2 needs higher-precision zeros or a different approach. Kim–Nguyen suggest that pruned enumeration could reach larger values much faster. (4) No improvement has been published since 2018, per Kim–Nguyen 2025 §4.2.

quantity: Upper bound for the least x with |M(x)| ≥ √x
statement: The least counterexample x to the Mertens conjecture satisfies x < exp(1.96·10^19). The criterion (Saouter–te Riele 2014) is that |h_StR(y)| > 1 + 6·10^{-8} implies x < exp(y + √y). BKZ-88 reduction followed by pruned lattice enumeration found h_StR(y) ≈ −1.007 at y ≈ 19,571,878,850,562,201,959.215107. Both h_P and h_StR were evaluated in Arb interval arithmetic. Zeros up to height 74,000 were computed in Arb to 300 digits, and Hurst's 10,000-digit data were used for the zeros up to height 14,000.

history.note: Pruned enumeration; exponent down 45 orders of magnitude since 1987

caveats: (1) Rozmarynowycz–Kim (arXiv 2305.00345v1) call their exp(1.017·10^29) 'an improvement over previously known exp(1.59·10^40) due to Kotnik and te Riele'. This omits Saouter–te Riele 2014's exp(1.004·10^33); Kim–Nguyen give the correct history. (2) Kim–Nguyen's bound lies below the Kotnik–van de Lune heuristic prediction x ≈ exp(5.15·10^23), so that heuristic is now contradicted. (3) Small refinements are possible: a referee's perturbed y gives h_StR ≈ −1.001, and Lemma E of StR14 gives x < exp(y + 2√(ky)). (4) The rigorous lower bound is x > 10^16 (Hurst), so the gap [10^16, exp(1.96·10^19)] remains huge. Johnston–Trudgian note that knowing the conjecture up to exp(10^19) would imply no simple zeros with β > 0.51 and γ < exp(10^16), 'indicative of the current futility of trying to precisely find the first counterexample'. (5) Data and code are deposited on Zenodo (record 10775723); I did not replay them.

quantity: Mertens-type and Skewes-type conjectures for L-functions other than ζ (number fields, function fields, prime races)
statement: Number fields: the natural analogue of the Mertens conjecture is false for all but finitely many number fields of any given degree, and the analogous Mertens function has a logarithmic limiting distribution (Hu–Kaneko–Martin–Schildkraut). Function fields: most hyperelliptic curves fail the Mertens-conjecture analogue, while a version with a larger constant holds for a positive proportion (Humphries). Prime races: generalized Skewes numbers for quadratic residue/non-residue races can grow very rapidly along highly composite moduli, which unconditionally disproves a conjecture of Fiorilli. Conditional upper bounds hold under GRH plus an effective LI (Bailleul–Hayani–Untrau 2026, preprint).
value: qualitative (falsity for almost all fields of fixed degree)
location: Abstracts / main theorems as summarized in arXiv metadata

history.value: number-field analogue false for all but finitely many fields of each degree

caveats: These results concern L-functions other than ζ and must not be read as statements about the classical M(x) or π(x) − li(x). Bailleul–Hayani–Untrau is unrefereed and its conditional part assumes GRH plus effective LI.

quantity: Growth of det(A_n) for the Redheffer matrix (A_ij = 1 if j = 1 or i | j)
statement: det(A_n) = M(n). Hence RH ⟺ det(A_n) = O(n^{1/2+ε}) for every ε > 0, and the Mertens conjecture in determinant form is false (Odlyzko–te Riele). Every quantitative frontier for det(A_n) is inherited from M(n): |det A_n| < √n for 1 < n ≤ 10^16 (Hurst). Recent spectral work: the vector w_k = Σ_{d|k} 1/d is provably close to the top singular vector (Clément–Steinerberger 2025).
value: inherits ARITH-MERTENS-RANGE / LIMSUP
location: Clément–Steinerberger abstract; det(A_n) = M(n) classical (Redheffer 1977)
caveats: The spectral facts sometimes quoted (spectral radius ~√n; eigenvalue 1 with multiplicity n − ⌊log2 n⌋ − 1; Barrett–Forcade–Pollington 1988, Vaughan 1993/1996) are from memory and unverified here. No spectral route has produced any bound on det(A_n) beyond what is known for M(n).

quantity: Upper bound for x_s, the first x ≥ 2 with π(x) > li(x)
statement: The interval [exp(727.951334744), exp(727.951336108)] contains more than 7.17·10^152 successive integers x with π(x) > li(x). The proof is a strengthened Lehman theorem plus computation over zeros. Hence x_s < exp(727.951336108) ≈ 1.397167·10^316.
location: Main result as summarized in zbMATH 6460495 (full text blocked by publisher bot-check)
caveats: (1) I could not open the full text, because the AMS site returned a bot-verification page. The interval endpoints come from the zbMATH review. The decimal conversion ≈ 1.397167·10^316 is mine. (2) Whether this region contains the first sign change is unknown. Stoll–Demichel 2011 (Math. Comp. 80, 2381–2394) propose a heuristic bound and from it claim 'the lower bound for Skewes' number is 3.17·10^114'. That is a heuristic, not a theorem; Büthe notes they also claimed x_s ≥ 10^18 without explanation. (3) Conditional context, from memory and unverified: Rubinstein–Sarnak 1994 give a logarithmic density of {π(x) > li(x)} of about 2.6·10^{-7} under GRH plus LI. (4) Related RH-equivalence: RH ⟺ ∫_2^x (π(t) − li(t)) dt < 0 for all x > 2 (Johnston, arXiv 2201.06184; abstract). (5) I found no improvement since 2015 in zbMATH or arXiv searches.

quantity: Lower bound for x_s (π(x) < li(x) verified for all 2 ≤ x ≤ X)
statement: li(x) − π(x) > 0 for 2 ≤ x ≤ 10^19. In addition: |x − ψ(x)| ≤ 0.94√x for 11 < x ≤ 10^19; x − θ(x) ≤ 1.95√x for 1423 ≤ x ≤ 10^19; x − θ(x) > 0.05√x for 1 ≤ x ≤ 10^19; and |li(x) − π*(x)| < √x/log x for 2 ≤ x ≤ 10^19. These follow from an analytic algorithm with expected cost O(x^{1/2+ε}), run with zeros up to height 10^11.
location: Theorem 2, eqs. (1.5)–(1.10), p. 2; numerical details §6 (pp. 11–12)

history.note: As cited by Büthe 2018 (paper on the first sign change of θ(x) − x)

caveats: (1) The computation used zeros up to 10^11 from Franke–Kleinjung–Büthe–Jost, given to accuracy 2^{-64}, in 64-bit fixed-point arithmetic. The text says round-off 'could be larger but can still be shown to be bounded by 0.016' with reference to Büthe's PhD thesis. The full rounding argument is therefore not in the paper. (2) Büthe 2016 (partial-RH method) was later 'corrected in the thesis of Sreerupa Bhattacharjee' (MSc, Lethbridge 2024), per Broadbent–Fiori–Kadiri–Ng–Wilk 2026 §1. I did not check whether this touches the 2018 algorithm. (3) The gap 10^19 < x_s < 1.397·10^316 is open, and I found no extension since 2018.

quantity: Best unconditional explicit bound of de la Vallée Poussin shape for |π(x) − Li(x)|, valid for all x ≥ 2
statement: |π(x) − Li(x)| ≤ 9.2211 x √(log x) exp(−0.84768363 √(log x)) for all x ≥ 2, where Li(x) = ∫_2^x dt/log t. The paper also proves |π(x) − Li(x)| ≤ 0.4298 x/log x for all x ≥ 2. Numerics use the zero-free constant R = 5.5666305.

caveats: (1) Since submission, the inputs have improved: R = 5.558691 (Mossinghoff–Trudgian–Yang, Res. Number Theory 10 (2024)), R = 4.896 (Bellotti–Trudgian–Yang, arXiv 2603.21490, unrefereed), new zero-density estimates (Farzanfard 2024) and Chirre–Helfgott (arXiv 2512.15709). source.title: Explicit bounds for the prime number theorem

verification.checked_against: Fiori–Jaskari arXiv 2609.23222v2: abstract, Thm 1.1 with the L(x0) table, eq. (1.6), Remarks 1.2–1.3, intro formula for ω(x), refs [2], [3], [21]; my high-precision recomputation of D.
verification.correction: The closed form is recoverable. D = (5/2)(5/3)^{1/5}(2000/161967)^{3/5}, with 2000/161967 = 2c/3 for c = 1/53.989. Equivalently D = (5^6 c^3/(2^2·3^4))^{1/5} = 0.19827677, which is exactly the asymptotic coefficient of ω(x) for the KV region quoted in FJ's intro. The draft's placeholder '(5/2)^{?}·(3/5)^{?}' has the wrong base (5/3, not 3/5).

The ω(x) '=' versus '∼' remark concerns Johnston 2411.13791 v1 and Bellotti's Bull. LMS paper, as stated. The bound is unrefereed.

quantity: Largest X for which Schoenfeld's RH-strength bound |π(x) − li(x)| < √x log x/(8π) is proved unconditionally on [2657, X]
statement: Unconditionally, |π(x) − li(x)| < √x log x/(8π) for 2657 ≤ x ≤ 1.101·10^26, and the weaker |π(x) − li(x)| < √x log x holds for 2 ≤ x ≤ 2.165·10^30. These rest on the rigorous verification of RH to height T = 3·10^12 (Platt–Trudgian; the precise height is H = 3,000,175,332,800) and refine Büthe's partial-RH method. Under full RH, Schoenfeld (1976, Cor. 1) proved the same bound for all x ≥ 2657. Lee–Nosal sharpen the RH-conditional ψ and θ bounds to √x log x (log x − log log x)/(8π) for x ≥ 101 and x ≥ 2657 respectively.
value: X = 1.101·10^26 (and 2.165·10^30 for the √x log x bound)
location: Corollary 3.3 and Theorem 4.1 (arXiv v2, §3–4); Büthe 2016 Thm 2 (Math. Comp. 85, 2483–2498); Lee–Nosal arXiv 2312.05628 Thm 1.2

history.value: bound for all x ≥ 2657 under RH

caveats: (1) Everything depends on the correctness of the interval-arithmetic RH verification to 3·10^12 (Platt–Trudgian, Bull. LMS 53 (2021) 792–797). (2) BFKNW (arXiv 2608.01498, §1) state that they use 'Büthe's method [Math. Comp. 2016] as corrected in the thesis of Sreerupa Bhattacharjee' (MSc, Lethbridge 2024). The nature of that correction was not checked here, and it may affect small-x constants. (3) Büthe's own relation (4.92√(x/log x) ≤ T) gives only 2.169·10^25 with T = 3·10^12. (4) Lee–Nosal's bounds are conditional on RH.

quantity: Explicit ψ error under a zero-free half-plane Re s > σ (quasi-RH)
statement: Suppose every zero ρ = β + iγ of ζ with β > 0 has β ≤ σ, where 3/4 ≤ σ ≤ 1. Then for x > x0 ≥ e^3, E_ψ(x) < A(x0) (log x)^2 x^{−1/4} + C(σ, x0) x^{σ−1}, with A and C tabulated. With σ = 7/8: E_ψ(x) < 0.04934 (log x)^2 x^{−1/4} + 0.02636425 x^{−1/8} for all x > e^3.
conditional_on: No zeros of ζ(s) with Re s > 7/8. The only claimed proof is the OpenAI 'Quasi-Riemann Hypothesis' announcement (Oct 2026), which is unrefereed. This archive's own architecture audit of the companion 11/12 paper found no verified error but lists unresolved ambiguities U1–U4, and the Lean formalization of the 7/8 theorem was not replayed.
location: Theorem 1.4 and the paragraph after its table, p. 5 of arXiv v2; proof §5.2
caveats: This is a conditional theorem inside an unrefereed preprint, and the hypothesis is itself only announced. It must not be cited as an unconditional explicit PNT bound. Even if the hypothesis holds, it settles none of Robin, Lagarias, Nicolas, Mertens or Skewes, which all need Re ρ = 1/2 or finer information.

quantity: Validity and best explicit bounds for the Mertens sums and products Σ_{p≤x} 1/p and ∏_{p≤x} p/(p−1). These are load-bearing for t-free Robin results and the Nicolas criterion.
statement: (i) Erratum chain. The main theorem (Thm 1.1) of Ramaré's explicit density estimate (Math. Comp. 85 (2016) 325–356) is incorrect: 'the stated leading constant … is off by a factor of over 100' (Broadbent–Kadiri–Lumley–Ng–Wilk 2021, §11 and footnote 3). As a result, the bounds in Dusart 2018 (Ramanujan J. 45, 227–251) are 'likely affected', in particular Thms 3.2, 3.3 and Table 1 (ψ) and Thm 4.2 and Table 2 (θ), as is Axler 2018 (Integers 18 A52) Thm 1.1. BKLNW Cor 11.2 gives valid proofs of Dusart's Thm 4.2. (ii) BFKNW (2026) state that the proofs of all of Dusart 2018's corollaries on Mertens sums and products are therefore invalid, that 'many authors have continued to use' them, and that BFKNW recover all of them. They prove, e.g., |Σ_{p≤x} 1/p − log log x − M| ≤ A_λ(x0) (log x)^{1/2} exp(−C√log x) with A_λ(2) = 9.2203 (Thm 2(i)), and two-sided bounds e^γ log x (1 − D_ℓ/(log x)^ℓ) ≤ ∏_{p≤x} p/(p−1) ≤ e^γ log x (1 + D'_ℓ/(log x)^ℓ) with tabulated D_ℓ, D'_ℓ (Thm 6).
value: A_λ(2) = 9.2203 (BFKNW Thm 2); Dusart 2018 Mertens corollaries: proofs invalid as published, restored by BFKNW (unrefereed)
location: BFKNW §1 remark 3 (pp. 4–5), Theorems 2 and 6 (pp. 3–5). BKLNW, Math. Comp. 90 (2021) 2281–2315 (arXiv 2002.11068): footnote 3 in §3 and the paragraph before Corollary 11.2.

Its published proof therefore inherits the gap until BFKNW, which is unrefereed. I did not check that this exact display is among the recovered statements. (2) Dusart 2018's π(x) expansion, π(x) = x/log x (1 + 1/log x + 2/log^2 x + O*(0.53816/log^2 x)) for x ≥ 11813 (zbMATH 6839074), is derived from the θ bounds. quantity: Rate of decay of the Báez-Duarte/Nyman–Beurling distance d_N (natural-number dilations, N terms)
statement: Unconditionally, liminf_{N→∞} d_N^2 log N ≥ Σ_{Re ρ=1/2} m(ρ)^2/|ρ|^2 (Burnol, improving Báez-Duarte–Balazard–Landreau–Saias, who had Σ 1/|ρ|^2 over distinct critical zeros). Under RH with simple zeros this constant is 2 + γ − log 4π = 0.0461914179…. Under RH, d_N^2 ≪_δ (log log N)^{5/2+δ}/√(log N) (Balazard–de Roton 2010). Under RH plus Σ_{|γ|≤T} |ζ'(ρ)|^{-2} ≪ T^{3/2−δ}, the choice V_N(s) = Σ_{n≤N} (1 − log n/log N) μ(n) n^{−s} achieves d_N^2 ~ (2 + γ − log 4π)/log N, so Burnol's lower bound is sharp (Bettin–Conrey–Farmer, Thm 1). RH ⟺ d_N → 0 (Báez-Duarte 2003).
value: d_N^2 ≥ (0.04619…+o(1))/log N unconditional lower bound (with simple critical zeros); conditional asymptotic equality
conditional_on: Upper bounds and asymptotics: RH (Balazard–de Roton); RH plus a bound on the second negative moment of ζ'(ρ) (Bettin–Conrey–Farmer)
location: Burnol Thm 1.3 (arXiv p. 3); BCF Thm 1 and intro (pp. 1–2); Balazard–de Roton main theorem (zbMATH 5758250)
caveats: (1) Numerics: Landreau–Richard (Exp. Math. 11(3), 2002) present numerical approximations of χ in the Nyman–Beurling space. I did not verify their N-range or precision. BCF remark that the Landreau–Richard graphs 'at first sight suggest that V_N is not optimal', in contrast with BCF's theorem. (2) Because of the unconditional lower bound d_N^2 ≳ 0.046/log N, finite computations of d_N can never show convergence to 0 and cannot decide RH. (3) I did not verify the BCF journal version (possibly Proc. Steklov Inst. 2013, from memory).

quantity: kappa* = liminf N0^s(T)/N(T) for zeta, unconditional (new pair-correlation/inertia method)
statement: Theorem A: as T -> infinity, N0^s(T,2T) >= (2/3 - o(1)) N(T,2T) and N_d(T,2T) >= (5/6 - o(1)) N(T,2T). With the Montgomery-Taylor window psi_MT in place of the indicator window, the constants become 2 - c_MT^{-1} = 0.67250... and (3 - c_MT^{-1})/2 = 0.83625.... A fortiori N0*, N0 and N^s are all >= (2/3 - o(1))N. The same holds on (0,T] with rate O(log log T/log T) (Remark 6.1). Theorem B: the same statement holds verbatim for L(s,chi), chi any fixed primitive Dirichlet character. Mechanism: Weil's explicit-formula Hermitian form is restricted to d ~ N(T,2T) modulated copies of a window. Each distinct on-line zero contributes a rank-one positive form, and each off-line pair {rho, 1 - conj(rho)} contributes a block of signature (1,1) (Sylvester inertia). The trace is (1+o(1))N. The squared Hilbert-Schmidt norm is (R(psi)+o(1))N, from Montgomery's prime-side second moment made unconditional by Aryan and by Baluyot-Goldston-Suriajaya-Turnage-Butterbaugh (BGST). A rank-trace inequality rank P1 >= 2 tr P1 + 4 tr Q' - 4b - ||P1+Q'||_HS^2 then gives N0^s >= (2 - R(psi) - o(1))N, with R(flat) = 4/3. No mollifier, zero-density estimate or zero-free region is used.
value: 2/3 (flat window); C_MT = 3/2 - (1/sqrt2) cot(1/sqrt2) = 0.6725007... (Montgomery-Taylor window)
location: Theorem A and Theorem B, pp. 1-2; mechanism §1.2, eqs. (1.1)-(1.2); Remark 6.1; limits §7.2; Lean statements in Appendix A, p. 15

history.note: secondary source: BCY intro and AF §1.3

caveats: (1) Unrefereed as of 2026-11-17. The paper reports a Lean 4 formalisation (anthropics/zeta-23-lean, tag v1.0, Mathlib 51e6992efd06) whose #print axioms returns only propext, Classical.choice and Quot.sound. We did not re-run it. (2) Dispute about the written proof: J. Arias de Reyna, arXiv:2610.24612 (§1.1 p. 3; footnote 1 p. 15), says that 'as it's written, [v2] doesn't work'. The boundary-zero contribution with U = sqrt(T) is bounded only by O(N), not o(N). He supplies a modified choice, judges the repair to need no more than a note, and asks how a paper with a Lean proof can contain false statements, which suggests the formal object and the printed text differ. No v3 has appeared (arXiv history checked 2026-11-17). (3) The abstract calls 5/12 the previous record for N0^s/N. In fact 5/12 is PRZZ's bound for kappa; their simple-on-line bound is 0.407511. (4) There is an independent human proof (Lamzouri, CRIT-02). (5) The method cannot reach 100% or RH as stated: its inputs are insensitive to o(N) off-line zeros, and they hold for the Davenport-Heilbronn and Epstein zeta functions, for which the analogue of RH fails (§1.4).

verification.checked_against: arXiv:2608.13637v2 full text: abstract; §1.1-1.4 (Theorems A and B); §2.2-2.3; Props 4.2-4.3; proof of Theorem A; Remark 6.1; §7.1-7.3; Remarks 7.1-7.2; Appendix A. arXiv API: v2 of 2026-08-19 is still the latest version. arXiv:2610.24612v1 §1.1 and footnote 1 p. 15.
verification.notes: Every constant, location and Lean detail checks out: tag v1.0, Mathlib 51e6992efd06, three standard axioms as reported by the repository's audit. Caveat (3) is correct. The abstract and §1.1 call 5/12 the previous record for N0^s/N, but PRZZ's kappa* is 0.407511. On the dispute, I located a concrete candidate for the step Arias de Reyna objects to. The proof of Prop. 4.2 asserts |Re gamma_rho - alpha_k| >= D_rho for k outside [0,d) for every zero with Re gamma_rho in I' = [T - sqrt T, 2T + sqrt T). That only holds for Re gamma_rho in I = [T,2T), not for zeros in I' minus I. This matches his footnote 1 ('In [1] U is taken equal to sqrt T. Their bound is of the order of N'). It looks repairable, either by U = T^theta with theta < 1/2 as he does, or by distance decay, so the wording 'a gap in the written proof' is right. Do not call the theorem false. The ledger's remark that the Lean object and the printed text 'differ' is the ledger's own inference. AF's second-moment theorem (Theorem 5.7) is proved inside the paper (Props 5.2-5.5), so AF does not depend on the BGST 2024 proof. In the history, Lamzouri's proof is a second proof written after AF, not an independent discovery (see CRIT-02).

quantity: Independent proof of kappa* >= C_MT, plus 'rigidity' bounds (simple OR on the line; average of the two proportions)
statement: Theorem 1.1: liminf N0^s(T)/N(T) >= C0 = 0.67250... and liminf N_d(T)/N(T) >= C1 := (C0+1)/2 = 0.83625.... Moreover liminf N_{s or 0}(T)/N(T) >= C2 = (1 + 2 sqrt2 + 2 C0)/(3 + 2 sqrt2) = 0.88762..., and liminf (N_s(T) + N0(T))/(2N(T)) >= C1. Here C0 = 3/2 - (1/sqrt2) cot(1/sqrt2). Consequences (Remark 1.2): at most 1 - C2 < 0.1124 of the zeros are both off the line and multiple, and max(N0, N_s) >= (C1 + o(1))N. The proof replaces the finite-dimensional matrix and rank-trace framework with a single Hilbert-space inequality, followed by Montgomery's pair-correlation theorem in the unconditional BGST form (Lemma 5 of BGST 2024). The optimisation leads to the same Montgomery-Taylor extremal problem (Remark 3.4).
location: Theorem 1.1 and Remark 1.2, p. 3
caveats: Unrefereed. The author thanks Conrey, Goldston, Gonek, Granville, Milinovich and Tenenbaum for reading a draft, which is not formal refereeing. The Lean certificates were produced afterwards by Axiom Math (Appendix A); we did not check them. This is the main independent human corroboration of CRIT-01. Under the narrow-box hypothesis, BGST Theorem 3(iii) gives the larger union constant (2 + C0)/3 = 0.89083 (CRIT-15).

source.title: A new proof that more than 2/3 of the zeros of the Riemann zeta function are simple and on the critical line

verification.checked_against: arXiv:2609.02882v2 full text: abstract, §1 (Theorem 1.1, Remark 1.2), Lemma 3.1 (= BGST 2024 Lemma 5), Remark 3.4, Acknowledgments, Appendix A, references. arXiv:2501.14545v3 §3 and footnote 2.
verification.correction: The Lean caveat must be strengthened. Appendix A says AxiomProver produced an UNCONDITIONAL certificate only for Proposition 2.1, the Hilbert-space inequality. The certificate for Theorem 1.1 was generated 'under the assumptions of [3, Lemma 5]' (the BGST unconditional pair-correlation lemma) and the Riemann-von Mangoldt asymptotic. So the formalisation does not check the analytic input. In addition, the proof of BGST 2024 (Acta Arith. 214) Theorem 1, on which Lemma 5 rests, contained an error in a lower-order term. quantity: Computer-assisted refinements: kappa*, N_d/N and N^s/N beyond the Montgomery-Taylor constant
statement: Theorem 1.3: liminf N0^s(T)/N(T) >= s0 = 1669159/2478195 = 0.67353820.... Theorem 1.1: liminf N_d/N >= 1645064/1960733 = 0.83900459675.... Corollary 1.2: liminf N_s/N >= 1329395/1960733 = 0.67800919 (simple zeros anywhere in the strip). Theorem 1.4: (N_s + N0)/(2N) >= 0.83676910 and N_{s or 0}/N >= 0.88916092. Theorem 1.5: N_{s or 0}/N >= 50652159/56956375 = 0.88931500. Method: unconditional pair-correlation 'energy'; a large-sieve inequality for zeros separated by a fixed fraction of the mean spacing; and a computer-assisted local inequality for 7 or 8 consecutive zeros that distinguishes simple from double zeros, with correction terms that telescope as a storage function.

caveats: (1) Unrefereed, and the bounds are computer-assisted. Lean proofs use three extra axioms, one per local inequality, each recording that a search program returned true; Lean's kernel does not check that run. The paper describes itself as an experiment in AI-assisted research. (2) It lists a swarm of unverified, unrefereed values for kappa* between 0.67300 and 0.673492 (GitHub repos, Zenodo drafts, the Riemann.fail list with Lean entries up to 0.67348). The largest, 0.673492, is a draft pull request (PR 888) to GettysburgResearch/riemann, the host repository of this Observatory. Under this project's rules it is an unreviewed branch claim and must not be counted as a result. (3) A Zenodo report by H. Yang and S. Yang claims 0.7962 simple-on-line and 0.8981 distinct from trace moments of order up to 6. Its own authors grade the analytic part as not yet verified, so it is excluded. (4) The author's earlier paper arXiv:2609.33043 proved N_d/N >= 0.8369928814 (relying on an unrefereed computer-assisted local inequality). (5) B. Wang's arXiv:2609.24167 (+6.67e-8) is withdrawn.

quantity: kappa (zeros on the line, with multiplicity) and kappa*: best REFEREED result, Levinson-Conrey mollifier method
statement: Theorem 1.2: more than five-twelfths of the nontrivial zeros of zeta are on the critical line. §8 gives the explicit values kappa >= 0.417293962 and kappa* >= 0.407511457. Setup: Levinson's method mollifying V(s) = zeta + lambda1 zeta'/log T (d = 1) with the generalised Feng mollifier (K = 3), of length theta = 4/7 - eps; R = 1.3036 for kappa and R = 1.1167 with linear Q for kappa*. Theorem 4.1 shows that N = T^{4/7-eps} is admissible for the twisted second moment with coefficients built from mu * Lambda^{*k}. §5.1 proves 'Feng's conjecture' that only square-free terms contribute to the main term.
location: Theorem 1.2, p. 8; numerics §8, p. 56; Theorem 4.1 (admissible length 4/7); §5.1 (Feng's square-free claim) (arXiv v3)

history.note: Lou's announced 0.35 never appeared with proof; secondary source (Feng intro)

caveats: This is the record of the mollifier method and the best refereed unconditional value. It is superseded numerically by the unrefereed CRIT-01 and CRIT-02 (0.6725 >= kappa* lower bound, hence also for kappa). The numerical optimisation is 'interim' and uses non-interval floating-point Mathematica-style evaluation of main-term constants. PRZZ say Feng's arXiv v1 obtained 0.417288, rounded to 0.4173, but with an unjustified length (CRIT-05). PRZZ remark that their results and Wu's Dirichlet-L analogue agree. Z. 293 (2019) 825-865 (arXiv:1802.09704, posted just before PRZZ), Theorem 1.2: kappa(chi) > .4172 and kappa*(chi) > .4074 for ANY Dirichlet character. The principal character gives zeta. PRZZ Remark 1.1 and Wu's closing remark both say the work was independent and the results agree, and Cobeli-Zaharescu credit 'Wu and independently PRZZ' with > 5/12. quantity: Disputed constant: Feng's kappa >= 0.4128 (and the earlier claim 0.4173)
statement: Feng (J. Number Theory 132 (2012)) proves Theorem 1: kappa >= 0.4128, using a two-piece mollifier with a Conrey piece of length theta = 4/7 - eps and Feng pieces of length theta1 = 1/2 - eps (I = 3, R = 1.3025). Corollary 1 states that the 'theta = 1' conjecture implies kappa >= 0.6107. Dispute: arXiv v1 of Feng's paper took all pieces of length 4/7 and claimed kappa > 0.4173 and kappa* > 0.4075. After Conrey queried this, Feng accepted the error and reduced the pieces to 1/2 (Bui, arXiv:1410.2433, Remark 1.1). BCY 2011 could not verify that Feng's mollifier may have length 4/7. With only the Balasubramanian-Conrey-Heath-Brown twisted second moment, the cross term needs theta1 + theta2 < 1, which gives theta2 < 3/7 and kappa >= 0.410725, kappa* >= 0.403211 (Kühn-Robles-Zeindler, J. Number Theory 174 (2017), Theorem 1.2). Resolution: Pratt-Robles (2018) proved that the Feng piece may have length 6/11 > 1/2, validating 0.4128 and giving 0.41491637. PRZZ (2020) then proved length 4/7 for the generalised Feng mollifier and recovered essentially Feng's v1 numbers (0.417293962 and 0.407511457). PRZZ §5 also notes that Feng's assertion that non-square-free terms contribute only lower order was an 'unproved claim'; they prove it in §5.1.
value: 0.4128 (Feng, now justified); 0.4173 (Feng v1, unjustified when posted; later effectively realised as 0.417293962 by PRZZ)
location: Feng: Theorem 1 (p. 5) and Corollary 1, §5 (p. 28) of arXiv v2. Kühn-Robles-Zeindler: Theorems 1.1-1.2, p. 3. Bui: Remark 1.1, arXiv:1410.2433. PRZZ: §1, pp. 7-8 and §5.

That makes it a conditional, unpublished note. Preobrazhenskii and Preobrazhenskaya (arXiv:1403.5786, abstract only) state 41.2948% 'assuming Feng's condition on the lengths', so it is conditional on the then-unproved length. Lesson for the archive: the 2010-2017 literature quoted 0.4128 as the record while its admissibility was in doubt.

quantity: Admissible mollifier length theta (y = T^theta) in the twisted second moment of zeta
statement: Unconditional admissible lengths for the twisted second moment int |zeta(1/2+it)|^2 |A(1/2+it)|^2 dt. Arbitrary coefficients a_n << n^eps: theta < 1/2 (Balasubramanian-Conrey-Heath-Brown 1985), improved to theta < 17/33 (Bettin-Chandee-Radziwill, Crelle 729 (2017) 51-79, via Bettin-Chandee trilinear Kloosterman bounds); Robles-Roy-Zaharescu get 48/95 by bilinear bounds. Conrey-type coefficients mu(n) P(log(y/n)/log y): theta < 9/17 (BCHB, Weil bound) and theta < 4/7 (Conrey 1989, Deshouillers-Iwaniec). Feng-type coefficients mu * Lambda^{*k}: theta < 6/11 (Pratt-Robles 2018, Theorem 1.2, via Type I/II decomposition and incomplete Kloosterman sums), then theta < 4/7 (PRZZ Theorem 4.1, using Vaughan/Heath-Brown identities). PRZZ remark (§9(3)) that additivity of log in (mu * log) is what allows 4/7, and ask how to lengthen without over-specialising the coefficients.
value: 4/7 (structured mollifiers, since 1989); 17/33 (generic coefficients)
location: PRZZ §1, pp. 7-8 and Theorem 4.1; Pratt-Robles Theorem 1.2, Remark 1.3 and §5 (kappa >= .41491637)
caveats: The values for BCHB (9/17), Conrey (4/7), BCR (17/33) and RRZ (48/95) are as reported in PRZZ's full text (secondary relative to the original papers, except that BCR's journal data were confirmed via zbMATH). No admissible theta > 4/7 for any mollifier that is useful for Levinson's method is known unconditionally; the 4/7 barrier has stood since 1989. Pratt-Robles corrected a misprint in the statement of their Theorem 1.2 in later arXiv versions (it was found by Heath-Brown).

statement: Feng, Corollary 1: if Lemma 2 and Theorem 2 (the twisted second-moment asymptotic for his mollifier) hold for every theta = theta1 < 1, then kappa >= 0.6107 (R = 0.7721, I = 3). In families the asymptotic large sieve makes theta = 1 available on average. Conrey-Iwaniec-Soundararajan, Theorem 1: for (log Q)^6 <= T <= (log Q)^A, N0'(T,Q) >= (14/25) N(T,Q) for the family of primitive Dirichlet L-functions, where N0' counts simple zeros on the line (kappa' = 0.56001 at theta = 1, r = 10/9, R = 0.83). Sono (arXiv:2105.07422, abstract) uses Feng's mollifier to get >= 61.07% on the line and >= 60.44% simple and on the line, on average over primitive characters and conductors.
value: 0.6107 (conditional on theta = 1 for zeta); 14/25 = 0.56 and 61.07% (family averages, unconditional)
conditional_on: Twisted second moment of zeta with Feng's mollifier of length T^{1-eps} (the 'theta = 1 conjecture' as Feng states it)
location: Feng Corollary 1, eq. (5.5), §5 p. 28 (arXiv v2); CIS Theorem 1, eq. (1.5), Crelle 681 (2013) 175-198 (arXiv:1105.1177); Sono abstract

history.value: 0.811 simple on line / 0.905 distinct (Dirichlet family average)
history.note: details omitted, not in Lean, unrefereed

caveats: Key comparison: even the conditional theta = 1 output of the Levinson-Conrey-Feng method (0.6107) is below the new unconditional pair-correlation value 0.6725 (unrefereed). The mollifier route is therefore dominated unless theta can be pushed well beyond 1. Sono's 61.07% coincides numerically with Feng's conditional 0.6107; we infer, without checking, that this reflects the same theta = 1 optimisation. Sono's result is abstract-only for us, and the metadata show no journal reference.

source.title: Zeros of the Riemann zeta function on the critical line

verification.checked_against: Feng arXiv:1003.0059v2 Corollary 1 (5.5): theta = theta1 = 1 - eps, R = 0.7721, I = 3. CIS arXiv:1105.1177 Theorem 1 (1.5), the computation kappa' = 0.56001 (theta = 1, r = 10/9, R = 0.83), and the Remarks. Sono arXiv:2105.07422 (abstract). AF §7.3 Remark 7.2.
verification.notes: Additions. CIS's own Remark gives kappa' = 0.5865 with the optimal sinh-type P (a = 1.3408, R = 0.75), which is why Wu (2019) cites CIS as 58.65%. Wu, Q. J. Math. 67 (2016) 757-779 later reached 60.261% simple for the family. AF's 0.811 / 0.905 sits in a remark with details omitted and outside Lean, so it is an announcement. The family-versus-individual distinction is correctly drawn. The statement that the theta = 1 output 'is dominated' applies only to Feng's specific mollifier, not to the method in general (see frontier critique).

quantity: Limits of mollification as theta grows (theta = infinity, lower bounds for mollified error)
statement: Radziwill, Theorem 1: there is an absolute constant c > 0 such that for every theta > 0, all large T and every M_theta(s) = sum_{n <= T^theta} a(n) n^{-s} with a(n) << n^eps and a(1) = 1, I(M_theta) = (1/T) int_T^{2T} |1 - zeta M_theta(1/2+it)|^2 dt >= c/theta. For theta < 1/2, c = 1 (Proposition B, Soundararajan). Theorem 2: under RH and the Pair Correlation Conjecture, I(M_theta) >= (1 + o_theta(1))/(0.5 + theta). Related: Farmer's 'theta = infinity conjecture' (Mathematika 40 (1993) 71-87) asserts that the Conrey mollifier keeps I ~ 1/theta for all theta and implies 100% of zeros on the line. Bettin-Gonek (Mathematika 63 (2017) 29-33) show that theta = infinity implies RH. Feng (2012, §1 remark (a)) notes that a positive proportion of zeros of zeta + zeta'/log T lie near the line under the small-gap conjecture, so 100% via Levinson needs R -> 0 or a different f(s).
value: I(M_theta) >= c/theta (unconditional); >= 1/(0.5 + theta) under RH + PCC
location: Theorem 1 and Theorem 2, Proposition B, pp. 1-2 (arXiv v3)
caveats: We could not locate a journal publication of Radziwill's paper (zbMATH lists only arXiv:1207.6583). Farmer's and Bettin-Gonek's statements come from secondary sources (Feng intro; PRZZ §1); zbMATH confirmed their bibliographic data only. Conrey-Farmer-Kwan-Lin-Turnage-Butterbaugh (arXiv:2508.11108, abstract) show that optimising the linear combination of derivatives gives a positive proportion for any mollifier length, however short. For short mollifiers this matters more than refining the mollifier. Dong-Wattanawanichkul-Zaharescu (arXiv:2605.24363, abstract) extend Bettin-Gonek to GL(m) automorphic L-functions.

source.title: Limitations to mollifying zeta(s)
source.venue: arXiv preprint (zbMATH indexes only the arXiv version)

verification.checked_against: arXiv:1207.6583v3 full text: Theorem 1, Proposition B, Theorem 2 and remark. zbMATH: 'Preprint, arXiv:1207.6583 (2012)' only. zbMATH: Farmer, Mathematika 40 (1993) 71-87. Bettin-Gonek bibliographic data via PRZZ [5]. Abstracts of arXiv:2508.11108 and 2605.24363.
verification.correction: Radziwill's paper is an unrefereed preprint, unpublished since 2012 as far as zbMATH knows. The status 'unconditional_theorem' should carry an unrefereed flag. Theorem 2 also assumes a(p^k) << 1, which the author says can be removed. The bound concerns Selberg-type mollification, I = (1/T) int |1 - zeta M|^2. Radziwill notes that c depends on the proportion of zeros on the line. It does not directly bound the Levinson proportion. So the use in CRIT-20(c) and in the frontier, that Levinson-type arguments 'cannot be pushed', is an overreach. The bound limits how fast I can decay, which is consistent with Farmer's theta = infinity scenario.
verification.notes: c = 1 for theta < 1/2 (Proposition B, Soundararajan) and the RH + PCC bound >= (1 + o(1))/(0.5 + theta) are both verified. Dong-Wattanawanichkul-Zaharescu also give a family version implying a quasi-RH.

quantity: Ceiling of the pair-correlation / rank-trace (bandwidth-one) method for kappa* and N_d/N
statement: Alpöge-Furman §7.2. A 'bandwidth-one certificate' depends on the configuration only through its first two trace moments against test functions with Fourier support in [-1,1] and through the split into on-line points and off-line pairs, and it satisfies p <= N0^s/N configuration by configuration. For any such certificate p <= p0 + 2.55e-6 (|r'(1)| + int|r''|) for band-limited windows, with p0 <= 0.6818287. This value is the exact rational of an explicit 256-periodic law, certified by interval arithmetic (EnclOK, not kernel-checked) plus Lean-checked inequalities. It is below 0.6819 for both windows used, so 2/3 is within 0.016 of the ceiling. Given only the trace, Hilbert-Schmidt norm and block structure, inequality (1.1) is sharp, and the extremal configuration is Montgomery's: 2N/3 simple on-line zeros plus N/6 doubles. The Montgomery-Taylor window is optimal among windows of the form 2 - R(psi) [CCLM17, Cor. 14]. Unconditionally, higher traces add nothing: the prime-side evaluation of tr G^k is available only for X^k <= T^{2-eps}. Conditionally, the hypothesis HL*(4) (Hardy-Littlewood-type additive correlations) would give kappa* >= 13/18, and HL*(k0) for all k0 would give 100%. Knausgård (§7 and Figure 2) gives ceilings for his refinement: inequalities for 8 consecutive points cannot exceed 0.67357; no pair-energy lower bound for simple points exceeds 0.67383 (Prop. 7.3, second window); any window satisfying V(f) <= 10 B(f) is capped at 0.68185 (Cor. 7.9). For distinct zeros the caps are 0.83916 (7 points), 0.83998 (any frame length) and 0.84093 (any regular window).
value: ceiling ~ 0.6818 (kappa*, bandwidth one); 0.84093 (N_d/N, regular windows)
location: Alpöge-Furman §1.4 and §7.2 (a)-(f), pp. 12-14; Knausgård §7.3-7.6, Proposition 7.2, Proposition 7.3, Corollary 7.9, Figure 2 (pp. 8-9)
caveats: These are rigorous-computation claims (interval arithmetic and Lean) inside unrefereed preprints. They bound the METHOD, not the true proportions. 'Bandwidth one' corresponds to Montgomery's F(alpha) being known only for |alpha| <= 1. For X >> T the off-diagonal prime sum needs prime-pair (Hardy-Littlewood) information, which Goldston-Montgomery show is equivalent to pair correlation beyond support 1. The two papers' ceilings agree (0.6818287 vs 0.68185).

source.authors: L. Alpöge, R. Furman; K. M. Knausgård
source.title: More than two thirds of the zeta zeros are simple and on the critical line; More than 83.9% ... distinct ...

verification.checked_against: AF arXiv:2608.13637v2 §1.4, §7.2(a)-(f), the bandwidth-one ceiling paragraph (Zeta23.PairCeiling, LawN256, EnclOK, p0 <= 0.6818287, 2.55e-6 term), §7.3. Knausgård arXiv:2610.08965 pp. 8-9, Props 7.1-7.3, Prop. 7.8 (period-256 law, p = 0.6818276195), Cor. 7.9.
verification.notes: Verified, with three refinements. (1) Knausgård's 0.68185 'rests on a construction of Alpöge and Furman', with the periodic law recomputed and certified by him. The agreement with AF's 0.6818287 is a re-certification of one construction, not two independent ceilings. (2) The 0.67357 (eight points) and 0.67383 (pair energy) caps are for Knausgård's second window only. The window-uniform cap for regular windows (V(f) <= 10 B(f)) is 0.68185. (3) AF state §7.2(d)-(f) 'informally', including HL*(4) giving 13/18 and that higher moments add nothing unconditionally. The 0.824|r(1)| term vanishes only for band-limited windows. EnclOK is checked by interval arithmetic, not by the Lean kernel, as the ledger says.

quantity: Proportion of simple zeros of zeta under RH (and GRH / GLH)
statement: Bui-Heath-Brown, Theorem: assuming RH, kappa* >= 19/27 (here kappa* = liminf N*(T)/N(T), N* counting simple zeros). Corollary: on RH, kappa_d >= 0.84665. This removes the Generalised Lindelöf Hypothesis from Conrey-Ghosh-Gonek (Proc. LMS 76 (1998) 497-522), using Heath-Brown's generalised Vaughan identity. Method: Cauchy-Schwarz on the first and second mollified discrete moments of zeta'(rho) over zeros. Pair-correlation route under RH (Chirre-Gonçalves-de Laat, Adv. Math. 361 (2020) 106926, Corollary 2): N_s >= (0.6792 + o(1))N under RH and 0.6845 under GRH, from N* <= 1.3208N (RH) and 1.3155N (GRH) in Theorem 1.
value: 19/27 = 0.7037... (RH); 0.6792 (RH, pair-correlation method); 0.6845 (GRH, pair-correlation method)
conditional_on: Riemann Hypothesis (BHB). RH or GRH for Dirichlet L-functions (CGdL). RH + Generalised Lindelöf Hypothesis (CGG 1998).
location: BHB: Theorem and Corollary, p. 1. CGdL: Theorem 1 and Corollary 2, §2 (arXiv:1810.08843).
caveats: Under RH every zero is on the line, so these are also kappa* statements. The best RH-conditional constant 19/27 exceeds the unconditional bandwidth-one ceiling 0.6818 (CRIT-10). An unconditional version of the CGG/BHB discrete-moment method would therefore beat that ceiling. RH enters BHB through the evaluation of sums over zeros as sums over real ordinates. No erratum found.

AMS 118 (1993) 365-372; CGG, Proc. LMS 76 (1998) 497-522.
verification.notes: All constants and attributions verified. The remark that 'an unconditional CGG/BHB would beat 0.6818' needs a qualifier: those methods bound simple zeros N_s anywhere. Unconditionally the comparator would be Knausgård's N_s >= 0.6780, not the kappa* ceiling, unless the method also yields on-line information.

quantity: Proportion of distinct zeros of zeta under RH
statement: Chirre-Gonçalves-de Laat, Corollary 3: assuming RH, N_d(T) >= (0.8477 + o(1))N(T), and 0.8486 under GRH. This combines BHB's 19/27 with N* <= 1.3208N and Montgomery's inequality 2N_s <= sum (m-2)(m-3)/m. Alpöge-Furman §7.3 (unrefereed): under RH the third trace tr G^3 is available [Hejhal; Rudnick-Sarnak]. Running their distinct-zero certificate with a cubic weight and BHB's 19/27 gives liminf N_d/N >= 0.85082.
value: 0.8477 (RH, refereed); 0.85082 (RH, unrefereed claim)
conditional_on: Riemann Hypothesis (GRH for the 0.8486 variant)
location: Corollary 3, §2 (CGdL); Alpöge-Furman §7.3, p. 14
caveats: The 0.85082 value appears only in a short paragraph of an unrefereed preprint and should be treated as an announcement. Under RH, Montgomery had 5/6, CGG 0.84568 (RH + GLH), BHB 0.84665, and Farmer-Gonek-Lee 0.8051 by pair correlation. The unconditional 5/6 of Alpöge-Furman matches Montgomery's RH constant. Note the variable naming: CGdL's N*(T) is a multiplicity-weighted sum, unlike BHB's N*(T), which counts simple zeros.

quantity: kappa* under hypotheses other than RH: thin-box hypotheses and the Pair Correlation Conjecture without RH
statement: Baluyot-Goldston-Suriajaya-Turnage-Butterbaugh (arXiv:2501.14545v3, Theorems 1-2): if for all large T every zero with T < gamma <= 2T satisfies |beta - 1/2| < b/(2 log T), then N0^s(B_0.3185) >= (0.66666908 + o(1)) (T/2pi) log T, which recovers the 2/3 proportion. With b = 0.001 the bound is 0.67250064. Goldston-Suriajaya (arXiv:2511.20059, 2603.28104) show that b = b(T) -> 0 gives 2/3 simple and on the line. Goldston-Lee-Schettler-Suriajaya (arXiv:2503.15449, abstract): Montgomery's Pair Correlation Conjecture alone, without RH, implies that asymptotically 100% of zeros are simple and on the critical line (Gallagher-Mueller method plus 'horizontal multiplicity'). The same holds under a form of the Alternative Hypothesis (arXiv:2507.06823). BGST 2024 (Acta Arith. 214, 357-376): if all zeros with T^{3/8} < gamma <= T lie within 1/(2 log T) of the line, at least 61.7% are simple.
conditional_on: Narrow vertical box hypothesis on all zeros (width b/log T), or Montgomery's Pair Correlation Conjecture (stated without RH), or the Alternative Hypothesis
location: Theorem 1 and Theorem 2 (eqs. for B_0.3185 and B_0.001), §1; Theorem 3 (horizontal multiplicity)

history.value: PCC (no RH) => 100% simple and on line

caveats: The 2/3 and 0.6725 box-conditional statements have been made unconditional by CRIT-01 and CRIT-02 (unrefereed). The PCC result is abstract-only for us and has no journal reference in the metadata. Nguyen (arXiv:2611.20347, 16 Nov 2026, abstract) extends the PCC approach to Artin L-functions under PCC and other conjectures.

quantity: Proportion of c-isolated zeta zeros (isolated implies simple and on the line), unconditional
statement: Theorem 1.1: let B0(T,c) count the zeros rho_n with min(gamma_{n+1} - gamma_n, gamma_n - gamma_{n-1}) > 2 pi c/log T. There is c > 0 with liminf B0(T,c)/N(T) >= 0.6552, and liminf B0(T,1/6)/N(T) >= 0.50875. Before this it was not known unconditionally that infinitely many isolated zeros exist. The method is an unconditional variant of Montgomery's pair-correlation method. The same paper shows at least 31% of zeros of a linear combination of two primitive Dirichlet L-functions with the same conductor and parity lie on the line with odd multiplicity; the previous value was 7.38e-9 (Dousselin).
caveats: Unrefereed. The author did not optimise the small-c proportion (Remark 1.2). This is qualitatively stronger than kappa*, since isolated zeros are simple and on the line.

statement: Theorem 1.1: more than 6.78% of the nontrivial zeros of zeta lie on the critical line; precisely kappa_0 > 0.0678190. The method is a mollified Selberg sign-change detector with coefficients lambda(n) of zeta^{-1/2} with profile powers v^{1/4} and v, plus rigorous interval computation (0.6779054 < C_{1/4} < 0.6786576). Correction: Zhuravlev's 1974 paper prints 2/21, but its logarithmic inequality drops a factor of 2 and its polar term has the wrong sign. The corrected benchmark is 2/(3 pi^2 e) = 0.0248493202 (eq. (4)).

location: Theorem 1.1, p. 1; eq. (4) and discussion, p. 2; §2.4 (Baluyot's Atkinson-type bound)
caveats: v2 itself corrected the proportion stated in v1 (we did not retrieve v1's value). The result is far below Levinson-type bounds; its interest is for L-functions where Levinson's method is unavailable. Baluyot's Atkinson-type method gives kappa_0 > 0.0001049 (0.0086729 if his fourth-moment estimates hold for mollifiers of any length), as reported there.

Wu arXiv:1802.09704 full text (Theorem 1.2: kappa(chi) > .4172, kappa*(chi) > .4074 'for any Dirichlet character', no primitivity needed). Abstracts of CIS Theorem 1, Sono, Hua-Yang 2608.16034 and 2609.27808, and CLLR 1211.6725.
verification.notes: Verified. Wu's theorem includes chi = 1, that is zeta itself, so it should also be cross-listed in CRIT-04 as a co-record. Missing from the family history: CIS Remark kappa' = 0.5865; Wu, Q. J. Math. 67 (2016) 60.261% simple; Hua-Yang arXiv:2609.27808 (the growing-height companion, with formula 2 - 1/c*_lambda for bandwidth lambda_bw <= 1). Hua-Yang's heights run from (log Q)^{1+eta}/Q up to Q^{A0} with Q = log q, unweighted over characters mod prime q.

quantity: Critical zeros of GL(2) and GL(3) L-functions (and Epstein zeta)
statement: Andersen-Thorner (Forum Math. 33 (2021) 477-491, abstract): at least 6.96% of the zeros of the L-function of any holomorphic or Maass cusp form lie on the critical line, by Levinson's method with Blomer-Harcos shifted-convolution bounds. Earlier: Hafner 1983 gave a positive proportion for level 1; Rezvyakova extended this to Gamma_0(D) (arXiv:1212.2948); Bernard 2015 and Kühn-Robles-Zeindler gave explicit small proportions. Conrey-Farmer-Kwan-Lin-Turnage-Butterbaugh (arXiv:2508.11108, abstract): optimised linear combinations of derivatives 'more than double' the modular proportions of Bernard and KRZ with the same arithmetic inputs. Conrey-Kwan-Lin-Turnage-Butterbaugh (arXiv:2607.00282, abstract): at least 1/9 of zeros of L(s, Pi_0 x chi), Pi_0 on PGL(3), averaged over primitive chi of conductor up to Q, lie on the line (unconditional for self-dual Pi_0). Rezvyakova (arXiv:2411.18492, abstract): Epstein zeta functions of integral binary forms have a positive proportion of zeros on the line.
value: >= 6.96% (each GL(2) cusp form); >= 1/9 (PGL(3) twist family)
location: Main theorem (abstract)
caveats: Abstract-level only. Alpöge-Furman's bandwidth-one pair-correlation argument might plausibly extend to GL(2), but no such statement was found in the sources read. Pair correlation for GL(2) at bandwidth one is a separate input. Epstein zeta violates RH, so a positive proportion there shows that the critical-line count does not detect RH.

source.title: Zeros of GL_2 L-functions on the critical line

verification.notes: All statements match the abstracts. Missing: CIS 2013 Theorem 3 gives, on average over twists, >= 7/20 simple on-line zeros for GL2 and >= 1/200 for GL3. CKLTB's 1/9 claims to remove the need for progress toward the Ramanujan conjecture, and its abstract says its PGL(2) results are 'quantitatively stronger', with no value given. Individual-form results (6.96%) must not be mixed with twist-family averages.

quantity: Unrefereed claims of 100% (or much larger) proportions: not accepted
statement: Preobrazhenskaya-Preobrazhenskii, arXiv:1805.07741v7 (math.GM, 1 Nov 2025), state 'Theorem 1. kappa = 1' (almost all zeros on the critical line). The approach is a Levinson-type method applying the AM-GM inequality and second-moment asymptotics only on a subset, with zero-density exponents of Jutila and Conrey and a Schwarz-Christoffel mollifier. Dumitrescu-Wolf, arXiv:2205.09042 (abstract), also claim almost all zeros are on the line. H. Yang and S. Yang (Zenodo 2026, cited by Knausgård) claim 79.62% simple-on-line.

location: Theorem 1, §1 (v7)
caveats: We read only the statement and abstract and did not audit the proof. Grounds for not accepting it: (a) seven versions over 2018-2025, listed in math.GM; (b) every 2026 paper read (Alpöge-Furman, Lamzouri, Knausgård, Pearce-Crump, Arias de Reyna) treats PRZZ's 5/12 as the unconditional record before August 2026; (c) Feng's remark (a) and Radziwill's c/theta bound (CRIT-09) show that Levinson-type arguments at finite length cannot simply be pushed to 100%. Listed only so that the ledger records these claims; do not cite them as results.

verification.checked_against: arXiv:1805.07741v7 (math.GM, 1 Nov 2025): abstract and Theorem 1 statement only. arXiv:2205.09042 metadata (math.GM; arXiv admin note: text overlap with 2102.08313). Knausgård ref. [50] (Yang-Yang Zenodo, 17 Aug 2026).

Radziwill's c/theta bound does not bound Levinson proportions (CRIT-09), and Feng's remark (a) is conditional on the small-gap conjecture. Reasons (a) and (b), together with the absence of any audit, are sufficient grounds for exclusion.

quantity: Existence and range of the de Bruijn–Newman constant Λ (classical ζ)
statement: Normalization used throughout this ledger (Polymath/Rodgers–Tao): H_t(z) = ∫_0^∞ e^{tu²} Φ(u) cos(zu) du, Φ(u) = Σ_{n≥1} (2π²n⁴e^{9u} − 3πn²e^{5u}) exp(−πn²e^{4u}), H_0(z) = (1/8) ξ(1/2 + iz/2). H_t solves the backward heat equation ∂_t H_t = −∂_zz H_t. Pólya: if H_t has only real zeros, so does H_{t'} for every t' > t. de Bruijn (1950): H_t has only real zeros for t ≥ 1/2. Newman (1976): there is an absolute constant Λ with −∞ < Λ ≤ 1/2 such that H_t has only real zeros if and only if t ≥ Λ. RH ⇔ Λ ≤ 0. Newman conjectured Λ ≥ 0, which he called a quantitative version of the dictum that RH, if true, is only barely so.
location: Newman 1976, main theorem, as restated in Rodgers–Tao arXiv:1801.05914v5 §1 p.2. de Bruijn 1950 Thm 13, as restated in Dobner arXiv:2005.05142 Thm 3 p.9.
caveats: I could not read the original PDFs because the AMS site returned a bot-check page. Watch the normalization: Ki–Kim–Lee (zbMATH 1175.30023) use Ξ_λ with Λ = 4λ^(0), and other papers use t/4 conventions. Every number in this ledger is in the H_t normalization above.

source.authors: C. M. Newman; N. G. de Bruijn
source.title: Fourier transforms with only real zeros (Proc. AMS 61 (1976) 245–251); The roots of trigonometric integrals (Duke Math. J. 17 (1950) 197–226)

verification.checked_against: Rodgers–Tao arXiv:1801.05914v5 full text, p.2 (restatement of Pólya, de Bruijn and Newman). Crossref metadata: Newman, Proc. AMS 61(2) 245–251 (Dec 1976); de Bruijn, Duke 17(3) (1950). zbMATH 0967.11034 review text, which also restates the result.
verification.notes: Statement and value are correct. The ledger-wide claim in the caveat that 'Every number in this ledger is in the H_t normalization' is false. Stopple's Λ_Kr (DBN-16) and the ACM function-field Λ_D values (DBN-18) use the variable s = 1/2 + ix, so their constants are Λ_H/4. See DBN-16. The RT bibliography gives Newman's pages as 246–251, but Crossref and zbMATH give 245–251, so the draft has it right. I did not read the original Newman or de Bruijn papers.

quantity: de Bruijn strip contraction (how an initial zero strip turns into an upper bound for Λ)
statement: Let φ be even and integrable with φ(u) = O(e^{−|u|^b}) for some b > 2, G(z) = ∫ φ(u) e^{izu} du, and G_t(z) = ∫ e^{tu²} φ(u) e^{izu} du. If every root of G lies in |Im z| ≤ Δ, then for t > 0 every root of G_t lies in |Im z| ≤ max(Δ² − 2t, 0)^{1/2}. Hence Λ ≤ Δ²/2. The classical strip 0 < Re ρ < 1 gives Δ = 1 and so Λ ≤ 1/2. A zero-free half-plane Re s > σ, combined with the functional equation, gives Δ = 2σ − 1 and so Λ ≤ (2σ−1)²/2. For σ = 7/8 this is Λ ≤ 9/32 = 0.28125 (Hakimoglu-Brown §1.1). My own arithmetic: σ = 11/12 gives Λ ≤ 25/72 ≈ 0.347, and beating 0.2 by this step alone would need σ ≤ (1+√0.4)/2 ≈ 0.8162.
value: Λ ≤ Δ²/2 for an initial zero strip of half-width Δ
location: de Bruijn 1950 Thm 13, as restated in Dobner arXiv:2005.05142 Thm 3 p.9. Used as Polymath arXiv:1904.12438 Thm 3.2. The σ = 7/8 conversion is in Hakimoglu-Brown arXiv:2610.12803 §1.1 p.2.
caveats: I did not open de Bruijn's original. The statement is quoted from Dobner's full text.

source.title: The roots of trigonometric integrals

verification.checked_against: Dobner arXiv:2005.05142v2 Thm 3 p.9 (full text) and Polymath arXiv:1904.12438v2 Thm 3.2 p.14, both restating de Bruijn Thm 13. Hakimoglu-Brown arXiv:2610.12803 §1.1 p.2. I recomputed all the arithmetic myself.
verification.notes: The conditions (φ even, O(e^{-|u|^b}) with b > 2) and the conclusion max(Δ²−2t,0)^{1/2} match Dobner's Thm 3. These conversions are all correct: Δ = 2σ−1; σ = 7/8 gives 9/32; σ = 11/12 gives 25/72 ≈ 0.347; and staying below 0.2 needs σ < (1+√0.4)/2 ≈ 0.8162. I did not read de Bruijn's original paper.

quantity: Strict upper bound Λ < 1/2 and asymptotic reality of zeros for t > 0
statement: Ki–Kim–Lee: Λ < 1/2, and for every t > 0 all but finitely many zeros of H_t are real and simple. Polymath later made this uniform (arXiv:1904.12438 Thm 1.5). For 0 < t ≤ 1/2, with C a sufficiently large and c a sufficiently small absolute constant: if x ≥ exp(C/t) and H_t(x+iy) = 0, then y = 0 and x = x_n + O(x^{−ct}) for some n. The function g(x,t) = (x/4π)log(x/4π) − x/4π + 11/8 + (t/16)log(x/4π) counts the zeros.
value: Λ < 1/2. For t > 0, H_t has only finitely many non-real zeros.
location: KKL main theorem and Theorems 1.3–1.4 (per zbMATH 1175.30023 and Polymath p.10). Polymath Thm 1.5, arXiv:1904.12438v2 pp.9–10 (full text read).

history.value: effective-form uniform version (Thm 1.5); explicit bound Λ ≤ 0.22

caveats: Secondary sources give only the strict inequality; I verified no explicit margin δ in Λ ≤ 1/2 − δ, and Rodgers–Tao call it 'sharpened slightly'. The constant C in Polymath Thm 1.5 is not explicit. The 2026 collision-exclusion claims use Thm 1.5(i) only in its qualitative form (remote reality).

source.title: On the de Bruijn–Newman constant

verification.checked_against: zbMATH 1175.30023 review text. Polymath arXiv:1904.12438v2 Thm 1.5 pp.9–10 and intro p.2 (full text). Crossref: Adv. Math. 222(1) 281–306.
verification.notes: The zbMATH review confirms Λ < 1/2 and that for every λ > 0 all but finitely many zeros are real and simple. It also records a KKL result the ledger omits: the derivative constants Λ^(m) are non-increasing in m and lim Λ^(m) ≤ 0 (see missing records). Polymath Thm 1.5 matches: 0 < t ≤ 1/2, g(x,t) with the 11/8 and (t/16) log(x/4π) terms, and x_n + O(x^{-ct}). KKL themselves work with Ξ_λ and Λ = 4λ^(0).

quantity: Zero dynamics of H_t under the backward heat flow (Csordas–Smith–Varga)
statement: For Λ < t (in particular Λ < t ≤ 0 if Λ < 0), the zeros of H_t are real, simple and avoid 0 (CSV Cor. 1). The positive zeros satisfy ∂_t x_k = 2 Σ_{j≠k} 1/(x_k − x_j) (CSV Lemma 2.4). This is a repulsion: zeros spread apart as t increases. A negative Λ would therefore forbid sufficiently close adjacent zeros ('Lehmer pairs') at t = 0, and the CSV criterion (Thm 1) turns a high-quality Lehmer pair into a lower bound for Λ. Polymath Prop. 3.1 extends the ODE to every simple complex zero at every t (symmetric-pair summation). A zero of multiplicity m ≥ 2 at t0 splits as z_j(t0) + √2 (t−t0)^{1/2} λ_j + O(|t−t0|), where λ_j are the roots of the Hermite polynomial He_m. CSV's own lower bound is Λ > −4.379×10⁻⁶.
value: ∂_t x_k = 2 Σ' 1/(x_k − x_j); CSV lower bound Λ > −4.379×10⁻⁶
location: CSV Cor. 1, Lemma 2.4 and Thm 1, as cited in Rodgers–Tao arXiv:1801.05914v5 pp.3–5 and p.11. Polymath arXiv:1904.12438v2 Prop. 3.1 pp.12–13 (full text).
caveats: The zbMATH review text is unavailable because of licensing, and I did not read the CSV original. The ODE as written is the Polymath/Rodgers–Tao version.

source.authors: G. Csordas, W. Smith, R. S. Varga
source.title: Lehmer pairs of zeros, the de Bruijn–Newman constant Λ, and the Riemann hypothesis

verification.checked_against: Rodgers–Tao v5 full text: p.7 cites [11, Corollary 1]; Theorem 11 cites [11, Lemma 2.4]; Table 1 p.3. Polymath v2 Prop. 3.1 pp.12–13 (full text), which cites [9, Lemma 2.4] = CSV. Crossref: Constr. Approx. 10(1) 107–129. The zbMATH review of CSV is unavailable for licensing reasons.
verification.notes: Small precision fix. In Rodgers–Tao (56), the sum in the ODE runs over all j ∈ Z* (it includes the mirrored zeros x_{−j} = −x_j) as a principal-value sum. It is not a sum over positive zeros only. The Hermite splitting statement and the CSV bound −4.379×10⁻⁶ match the secondary sources. I did not read the CSV original.
