statement: Found a new Lehmer pair of ζ zeros, which gives Λ > −1.14541×10⁻¹¹. This was the record lower bound until Rodgers–Tao proved Λ ≥ 0.
value: Λ > −1.14541×10⁻¹¹ (now superseded by Λ ≥ 0)
location: Abstract/main result (zbMATH 1267.11094 summary). Rodgers–Tao arXiv:1801.05914v5 Table 1 p.3.
caveats: The secondary sources disagree on one row. Rodgers–Tao Table 1 lists Odlyzko 2000 as −2.63×10⁻⁹, while the zbMATH review 0967.11034 of Odlyzko's paper says −2.7×10⁻⁹. Odlyzko's PDF failed TLS verification, so I could not settle it. Rodgers–Tao round SGD to −1.15×10⁻¹¹. I did not examine the rounding model of these published Lehmer-pair computations. All of these bounds are superseded by DBN-06.

source.authors: Y. Saouter, X. Gourdon, P. Demichel
source.title: An improved lower bound for the de Bruijn–Newman constant

verification.checked_against: zbMATH 1267.11094 summary (Λ > −1.14541×10⁻¹¹). Crossref: Math. Comp. 80(276) 2281–2287. Rodgers–Tao Table 1 p.3. zbMATH 0967.11034 review of Odlyzko 2000.
verification.notes: The record is historical and correctly marked as superseded by DBN-06. The Odlyzko 'discrepancy' is not a contradiction: −2.63×10⁻⁹ (RT table) is the stronger bound and implies −2.7×10⁻⁹ (the zbMATH review wording), so the review probably just rounds outward. The primary PDF is still unread: the umn.edu fetch failed TLS verification and the web-archive copy reset the connection. The history list is ordered by publication date, as in RT, which is why 1992 appears before 1991.

quantity: Newman's conjecture for ζ: lower bound Λ ≥ 0
statement: Theorem 1: Λ ≥ 0. Combined with RH ⇔ Λ ≤ 0, this gives RH ⇔ Λ = 0. The proof is by contradiction. Assuming Λ < 0 (and RH, which is harmless for this purpose), the CSV dynamics on Λ/4 ≤ t ≤ 0, together with Riemann–von Mangoldt-type counts for H_t and a Hamiltonian/energy monotonicity (∂_t H = −4E for the formal gradient flow), force the zeros of H_0 into local equilibrium. Concretely, x_{j+1}(0) − x_j(0) = (4π + o(1))/log T for a fraction 1 − o(1) of j ∈ [T log T, 2T log T]. This contradicts the Conrey–Ghosh–Goldston–Gonek–Heath-Brown small-gap theorem: for any λ > 0.77, a positive proportion of gaps are ≤ λ·4π/log T. Montgomery's pair correlation would also suffice.
value: Λ ≥ 0, so RH ⇔ Λ = 0
location: Theorem 1, p.3 (arXiv v5). Contradiction step in §9, pp.59–60. Section 8 energy estimates, footnote 16 p.55.

history.value: independent proof; extended to the extended Selberg class

caveats: Erratum-type note: arXiv v5 (3 Jul 2021) says it is 'the published version, but with some corrections to Section 8' after Ofer Zeitouni pointed out that the treatment of boundary contributions to the energy was inadequate (footnote 16 p.55). Crossref shows no registered erratum on 10.1017/fmp.2020.6 (checked 2026-11-17). Dobner's independent proof (DBN-07) makes the conclusion robust. Separately, an unrefereed preprint (A. Gershon, Preprints.org, 22 Apr 2026, doi 10.20944/preprints202604.1513.v1, 'The De Bruijn-Newman Constant Is Zero') claims Λ = 0, which is equivalent to RH. I read only its abstract. It is unverified and not accepted, and RH remains open.

source.title: The de Bruijn–Newman constant is non-negative

verification.checked_against: arXiv:1801.05914v5 full text: Thm 1 p.3; §9 pp.59–60, eq. (93) and the CGGGHB λ > .77 statement; ∂_t H = −4E eq. (6); footnote 16 p.55 (Zeitouni). arXiv API comment for v5. Crossref: Forum Math. Pi 8, e6 (2020).
verification.notes: Everything checks. The arXiv v5 comment confirms 'published version, but with some corrections to Section 8 … treatment of the boundary contributions to the energy was previously inadequate'. So the journal version of record contains the uncorrected §8, and Crossref lists no erratum. Dobner's independent proof (DBN-07) covers the conclusion. The CGGGHB small-gap input is used under RH, which can be assumed without loss of generality because Λ < 0 implies RH.

quantity: Generalized Newman conjecture: Λ_F ≥ 0 for every F in the extended Selberg class S♯
statement: Thm 1: for every F ∈ S♯ there is a real number Λ_F such that all zeros of ξ_t^F lie on the critical line iff t ≥ Λ_F. Thm 2: Λ_F ≥ 0 for every F ∈ S♯. This includes ζ and every primitive Dirichlet L-function. The proof uses no information about ζ zeros. For each t < 0, ξ_t(J_t(s)) ≈ [gamma-like factor]·ζ_t(s) with ζ_t(s) = Σ exp((t/4) log² n) n^{−s} (Thm 4), and a Bohr-type almost-periodicity theorem then shows that ξ_t has infinitely many zeros off the critical line.
value: Λ_F ≥ 0 for all F ∈ S♯; for t < 0 there are infinitely many off-line zeros
location: Theorems 1–2, p.3. Theorem 3 (de Bruijn), p.9. Theorem 4 and §3.1 (deduction of Thm 2).

history.value: framework for automorphic and function-field analogues

caveats: S♯ requires a Dirichlet series, meromorphic continuation and a functional equation, but no Euler product. This number-field setting differs from function fields, where individual Λ_D can be −∞ (DBN-18). Dobner gives no upper bounds on Λ_F beyond what de Bruijn's strip argument yields.

source.title: A proof of Newman's conjecture for the extended Selberg class

verification.checked_against: arXiv:2005.05142v2 (10 Jan 2026, 'updated to match the published version') full text: Thms 1–2 p.3, Thm 3 p.9, Thm 4 and §3.1, S♯ definition pp.6–8. Crossref and arXiv journal_ref: Acta Arith. 201(1) 29–62 (2021), doi 10.4064/aa200603-23-7.
verification.notes: Dobner's ξ_t^F((1+iz)/2) = ∫e^{tu²}Φ_F(u)e^{izu}du agrees with the H_t normalization, so for ζ his Λ_F equals the RT Λ. The value −1.12929×10⁻⁷ in the history list is in Stopple's normalization, not H_t (see DBN-16).

quantity: Polymath15 upper bound Λ ≤ 0.22 and the upper-bound criterion
statement: Thm 1.2 (criterion). Suppose t0, X > 0 and 0 < y0 ≤ 1 satisfy three conditions. (i) ζ(σ+iT) ≠ 0 for (1+y0)/2 ≤ σ ≤ 1 and 0 ≤ T ≤ X/2 (RH verified to height X/2). (ii) H_{t0}(x+iy) ≠ 0 for x ≥ X + √(1−y0²) and y0 ≤ y ≤ √(1−2t0) (canopy). (iii) H_t(x+iy) ≠ 0 for X ≤ x ≤ X + √(1−y0²), √(y0² + 2(t0−t)) ≤ y ≤ √(1−2t), 0 ≤ t ≤ t0 (barrier). Then Λ ≤ t0 + y0²/2. Thm 1.1: Λ ≤ 0.22, obtained with t0 = 0.2, y0 = 0.2, X = 6×10¹⁰ + 83952 − 0.5 and Platt's interval-arithmetic RH verification to 3.06×10¹⁰. The offset 83952 makes a partial Euler product over p ≤ 11 large. The authors say the canopy (ii) was the numerical bottleneck.
location: Thm 1.1 and Thm 1.2, p.2. Parameter choice §8.1, p.37. Claim verification §8.2–8.5. Effective Riemann–Siegel approximation Thm 1.3.
caveats: The barrier verification used Taylor-expansion 'stored sums' with a 20-decimal-digit target accuracy and conservative derivative bounds (p.48–49). The code is in the arb/ and pari/ directories of github.com/km-git-acc/dbn_upper_bound. I did not replay it.

source.title: Effective approximation of heat flow evolution of the Riemann ξ function, and a new upper bound for the de Bruijn–Newman constant

verification.checked_against: arXiv:1904.12438v2 full text: Thm 1.1, Thm 1.2 (i)–(iii) p.2; parameter choice and the 83952 / p ≤ 11 Euler-product remark p.3; §8.2 (Platt 3.06×10¹⁰); §8.4 'stored sum' with a 20-decimal target pp.48–49; github arb/ and pari/ directories.
verification.notes: All three hypotheses are transcribed correctly, and t0 + y0²/2 = 0.22. The 'canopy is the bottleneck' remark (p.3) holds for the X ≈ 6×10¹⁰ run. At the larger X of §10, the paper says the barrier is 'by far the most numerically intensive step'.

quantity: Upper bounds on Λ conditional on further RH verification (Polymath Table 1), and the expected 1/log T scaling
statement: Polymath Table 1 lists pairs of a barrier location X and parameters (t0, y0) for which hypotheses (ii) and (iii) of Thm 1.2 were verified numerically, each giving Λ ≤ t0 + y0²/2 provided RH is verified to height X/2. Sample rows: X = 2×10¹²+129093 gives 0.21; X = 5×10¹²+194858 (t0 = 0.186, y0 = 0.16733) gives 0.20; X = 2×10¹³+131252 gives 0.19; X = 6×10¹³+123375 gives 0.18; X = 3×10¹⁴+188911 gives 0.17; X = 2×10¹⁵+122014 gives 0.16; X = 7×10¹⁵+68886 gives 0.15; X = 6×10¹⁶ gives 0.14; X = 6×10¹⁷ gives 0.13; X = 9×10¹⁸ gives 0.12; X = 2×10²⁰ gives 0.11; X = 9×10²¹+70686 gives 0.10. So Λ ≤ 0.1 would follow from RH verified to about 4.5×10²¹. The authors' heuristic is that RH verified to height T gives Λ ≤ O(1/log T). An off-line zero at height T with y ≍ 1 moves at speed ≍ log T, so the bound cannot be improved substantially without excluding RH violations at height T or 'a massive expansion of the known zero-free regions'.
value: Λ ≤ 0.21 … 0.10, depending on the RH verification height (X/2 ≈ 10¹² … 4.5×10²¹)
conditional_on: RH numerically verified up to height X/2 for the chosen row, and correctness of the §10 barrier/canopy computations
location: §10 'Further numerical results': heuristic on pp.62–63, Table 1 'Conditional Λ Results' on p.64, computation remarks on pp.66–67.
caveats: §10 says the mesh points were computed to 20 digits, except for the two highest rows (10 digits), and that the two largest runs used a BOINC volunteer grid. The text does not explicitly state outward-rounded interval enclosures for these rows, so their certification level is less transparently documented than §8. The O(1/log T) scaling is a heuristic, not a theorem. My own arithmetic gives an implied constant t·log X of about 5.0–5.9 across the table.

quantity: Collision-exclusion upper bound for Λ (unrefereed, full text read)
statement: Claim: Λ < 156821/10⁶ = 0.156821. The only external inputs are Polymath Thm 1.3, eqs. (20)–(24), Thm 3.2 and Thm 1.5(i), plus the Platt–Trudgian height 3,000,175,332,800 and the bound Λ ≤ 1/5. The method excludes collisions of real zeros, meaning simultaneous vanishing of (H_t(x), ∂_x H_t(x)), for all real x and all t ∈ [0.156821, 0.2]. Three regions are handled separately: the compact interior up to a stationary separator at X = 6000000185827, a finite exterior X ≤ |x| ≤ W = 72382294738709 using five stable prime-polynomial Gram sources, and an Euler-product barrier for |x| ≥ W. Remote reality then forces any positive critical time to produce a finite multiple real zero. The certificate uses 664,505 Fourier coefficients, 44,182 torus boxes, 184 separator moments and 17,385 separator rectangles.
value: Λ < 0.156821 (claimed)
location: Eq. (3), p.3. Table 1, p.2. §2.1–2.2, pp.3–4. Certificates in GitHub release certificates-0156821-v1, commit 18dbc01ea36bf9a24d8f79822b5ce06b545e4ace.
caveats: This is a draft that has not been refereed. The authors identify a Cauchy–Schwarz obstruction intrinsic to the four-prime source family, which explains the narrow feasibility margin. Their Table 1 is a useful status classification of the whole 2026 cluster (U/CA/C7/8 and P/R labels). I did not replay any certificate.

quantity: Generalized constant for quadratic Dirichlet L-functions (Stopple's Λ_Kr)
statement: Λ_Kr = sup{Λ_{−D} : −D fundamental} for the heat deformation of quadratic Dirichlet L-functions L(s, χ_{−D}). For t ≥ Λ_Kr all of these L-functions have only critical-line zeros. Under GRH, Λ_Kr ≤ 0, and Stopple conjectures 0 ≤ Λ_Kr. Theorem 3: −D = −175990483 satisfies the low-discriminant criterion (15), so −1.12929×10⁻⁷ < Λ_Kr. Theorem 2: infinitely many discriminants satisfying (15) would imply 0 ≤ Λ_Kr, which random matrix theory predicts.
value: Λ_Kr > −1.12929×10⁻⁷ (superseded by Dobner: Λ_χ ≥ 0 for each primitive χ)
location: Theorem 3, p.18. Theorem 2, p.14. Definition of Λ_Kr, p.~5.

quantity: Non-trivial upper bounds Λ_L < 1/2 for Dirichlet L-functions (real primitive characters)
statement: Theorem 1.1: let χ_m be a primitive real character with conductor 3 ≤ m ≤ 400, and suppose every zero z of H_0^L satisfies |Im z| ≤ D for some 0 < D ≤ 1. Then Λ_L ≤ min(D²/2, Λ*(m, χ_m; D)), where Λ* is the infimum of t0 + y0²/2 over verified admissible triples. With D = 1 (unconditional): Λ_L ≤ 953/3200 = 0.2978125 for every such character, with stronger individual bounds in the appendix. The method extends Polymath's effective approximation with explicit conductor dependence and uses Platt's GRH verification to height h_m = 10⁸/m. Results for D < 1 are conditional, e.g. D = 3/4 under the 7/8 half-plane.
value: Λ_L ≤ 0.2978125 for all real primitive χ with conductor 3 ≤ m ≤ 400 (claimed)
location: Theorem 1.1, p.5. Remark 3.1 (initial-strip hypotheses). §6.10 (proof of Thm 1.1). §7 (numerics).
caveats: Unrefereed. The authors say these are the first non-trivial upper bounds for a Dirichlet L-function; before this only de Bruijn's 1/2 was known. The bounds are weaker than for ζ because the GRH verification height (10⁸/m) is far below 3·10¹². Nothing is claimed for complex characters or for conductors above 400. I did not replay the interval computations.

quantity: Newman constants for function-field L-functions
statement: Over F_q[T], RH (Weil) gives Λ_D ≤ 0 for every quadratic L(s, χ_D), and Λ_D can equal −∞. Newman's conjecture is therefore replaced by a family version, sup_{D∈F} Λ_D = 0. Andrade–Chang–Miller Thm 1.9: for squarefree D ∈ Z[T] of degree 3, Λ_{D_p} = log(|a_p(D)| / (2√p)), and Sato–Tate (non-CM case) gives sup_p Λ_{D_p} = 0. They also show that the Lehmer-pair lower-bound technique is insufficient for linear combinations of L-functions. Chang–Mehrle–Miller–Reiter–Stahl–Yott Thm 1.7: for q an odd prime power and a family F of monic squarefree D of odd degree ≥ 3 with (x^q − x, q) ∈ F, sup Λ_D = max Λ_D = 0, attained because Λ_D = 0 iff the L-function has a double root.
value: Λ_D ∈ [−∞, 0]; family supremum = 0 (attained for the families above)
location: ACM Conjecture 1.8 and Theorem 1.9, p.4. Chang et al. Theorem 1.7 and Corollary 1.8, p.3.
caveats: I did not verify the journal publication of Chang et al. In function fields an individual L-function can have Λ_D < 0, so the individual Newman statement can fail. This contrasts with Dobner's Λ_F ≥ 0 for every F ∈ S♯ over number fields.

quantity: Total positivity of the de Bruijn–Newman kernel (negative result)
statement: Theorem 1.1: K(u) = Φ(|u|) is not a Pólya frequency function of order 5. Eight further configurations are certified by two methods. The lower determinants D_2, D_3, D_4 are positive at the central configuration, but this does not establish PF_4 globally.

verification.checked_against: arXiv:2602.20313v2 full text: abstract; 'Changes in version 2'; Thm 1.1, Thm 1.2, Remark 1.3; §5.1; §6.1.

For context: failure of PF_∞ follows already from Schoenberg's characterization, because the bilateral Laplace transform of K is entire with zeros and so cannot be 1/Ψ. Only the specific order 5 is new. Total positivity of K is also not the positivity notion that RH needs (real-rootedness of its Fourier transform), so the result's relevance to Λ is marginal, as the draft says.

quantity: Analogue of Λ for the integral of ξ (a functional-equation family with no finite constant)
statement: For a one-parameter family of Fourier integrals satisfying a functional equation, which includes the integral of the Riemann ξ-function, members have only finitely many zeros on the critical line, and the zeros lie arbitrarily far from it. The de Bruijn–Newman analogue for this family is infinite.

location: Abstract (main theorems not located in full text).
caveats: This is a cautionary example: a functional equation alone does not give a finite constant, because de Bruijn's bound needs an initial zero strip. Dobner's S♯ framework supplies that strip through the Dirichlet-series axioms.

quantity: Lindelöf exponent upper bound mu(1/2) for classical zeta (unconditional, ineffective)
statement: For every eps>0, zeta(1/2+it) << |t|^{13/84+eps} as |t|->infinity; equivalently mu(1/2) <= 13/84, where mu(sigma)=limsup_{|t|->inf} log|zeta(sigma+it)|/log|t|. Also (13/84+eps, 55/84+eps) is an exponent pair (Thm 6). Proof route: a decoupling inequality for curves gives the essentially sharp sixth-moment mean value A_6 << N^{6+eps}, which solves Huxley's 'first spacing problem' optimally (Corollary 3). This is combined with existing treatments of the 'second spacing problem' (Huxley-Watt, Huxley) inside the Bombieri-Iwaniec method. Theorem 4 gives |S| << M^{1/2} T^{13/84+eps} for sums of length M=T^alpha with 17/42 <= alpha <= 1/2. Huxley [H1, Thm 3] and the exponent pair (1/9,13/18) cover 13/42 < alpha < 17/42.

quantity: RH-conditional Omega results for S(t), S_1(t) and the iterates S_n(t)
statement: Assume RH and fix beta in [0,1). Bondarenko-Seip (Thm 2): there exist c, c1 > 0 such that max_{T^beta<=t<=T} |S(t)| >= c sqrt(log T log_3 T/log_2 T) and max_{T^beta<=t<=T} S_1(t) >= c1 sqrt(log T log_3 T/(log_2 T)^3). Chirre-Mahatab (Thm 1, RH, 0<beta<1): max_{T^beta<=t<=T} ±S(t) >= c sqrt(log T log_3 T/log_2 T), so S(t) = Omega_±(sqrt(log t log_3 t/log_2 t)). Zhao 2026 (Cor. 1.2, RH): for every fixed n >= 0, max_{T^beta<=t<=T} epsilon S_n(t) >= c_{n,beta} (log T)^{1/2}(log_3 T)^{1/2}/(log_2 T)^{n+1/2} for epsilon = ±1.
value: Order sqrt(log T log_3 T/log_2 T) for S(t), with unspecified constants
conditional_on: Riemann Hypothesis
location: BS Theorem 2, eqs. (4)-(5), p.3; Chirre-Mahatab arXiv 1904.11051 Theorem 1 (Bull. LMS); Zhao arXiv 2611.19383 Theorem 1.1 and Corollary 1.2

|S| gains a sqrt(log_3) factor (one-sided in sign)
Two-sided Omega_± with the log_3 gain

history.note: Unrefereed; fills the missing sign direction for odd n

caveats: The Chirre-Mahatab arXiv comment says a mistake in an earlier version was corrected and A. Chirre was added as coauthor (v4, to appear in Bull. LMS). Zhao 2611.19383 is an unrefereed preprint from 3 days before this snapshot. Inoue-Kobayashi-Toma (arXiv 2510.14309, RH) give explicit-constant extreme values of S(t+h)-S(t) for h in [C/log T, c/log log T]; I did not extract their constant. The Farmer-Gonek-Hughes conjecture (GROWTH-16) puts the truth near sqrt(log t log log t), far above these lower bounds.

quantity: Maximum of |zeta| on random short intervals: Fyodorov-Hiary-Keating upper tail
statement: There exists C > 0 such that for any T >= 3 and y >= 1: (1/T) meas{T <= t <= 2T : max_{|h|<=1} |zeta(1/2+it+ih)| > e^y log T/(log log T)^{3/4}} <= C y e^{-2y}. The bound is expected to be sharp for y = O(sqrt(log log T)).
value: Order log T/(log log T)^{3/4}; tail y e^{-2y}
conditional_on: none
location: Theorem 1, p.2 (arXiv v2)

history.value: Conjecture: max = log T/(log log T)^{3/4} e^{M_T}, with M_T converging in law and tail ~ C y e^{-2y}
history.note: Random matrix and log-correlated field heuristics, with numerics

history.value: First order: max_{|h|<=1} log|zeta| ~ log log T
Sharp upper tail <= C y e^{-2y}
Upper bound on mesoscopic intervals |h| <= (log T)^theta, theta in (-1,0]

caveats: This concerns typical short windows (|h|<=1 around a random t in [T,2T]). It says nothing about max_{t<=T} |zeta| (GROWTH-10, GROWTH-16). The proof is an iterative upper/lower barrier scheme driven by twisted second and fourth moments. Ouimet (arXiv 2611.01905, Nov 2026, unrefereed) claims Gumbel convergence in law of the recentered maximum slightly to the right of the line (sigma -> 1/2 at an explicit rate) on expanding windows |h| <= (log T)^theta, theta > 0. That is not the critical-line FHK statement.

quantity: Fyodorov-Hiary-Keating: lower tail and tightness of the short-interval maximum
statement: Theorem 1: there exists c > 0 such that for T >= 100 and 0 <= y <= (log log T)^{1/10}, (1/T) meas{T<=t<=2T : max_{|h|<=1} |zeta(1/2+it+ih)| < e^{-y} log T/(log log T)^{3/4}} <= c^{-1} y^{-c}. Corollary 1 (with Part I): for every eps > 0 there is C such that, for t in a set of measure >= (1-eps)T in [T,2T], |max_{|h|<=1} log|zeta(1/2+it+ih)| - (log log T - (3/4) log log log T)| <= C; subsequential limits in law exist. Theorem 2: for any C>0 there is c>0 such that for 10 <= y <= C log log T/log log log T, P(max_{|h|<=1} |zeta| > e^y log T/(log log T)^{3/4}) >= c y e^{-2y} e^{-y^2/log log T}, matching the upper tail.

conditional_on: none

quantity: Selberg central limit theorem for log|zeta(1/2+it)|
statement: For each fixed real V, as T -> infinity: (1/T) meas{T <= t <= 2T : log|zeta(1/2+it)| >= V sqrt((1/2) log log T)} ~ (1/sqrt(2pi)) int_V^inf e^{-u^2/2} du. That is, log|zeta(1/2+it)| is approximately normal with mean 0 and variance (1/2) log log T.

conditional_on: none
location: Theorem 1, p.1 (new short proof of Selberg's 1946 theorem); Propositions 1-2

history.value: CLT for log zeta(1/2+it) (log|zeta| and arg)

caveats: This is a distributional theorem about typical t. It gives no pointwise growth bound. Gaussian behaviour beyond the standard-deviation scale is in GROWTH-15.

quantity: Large deviations of log|zeta(1/2+it)| at scale V ~ alpha log log T
statement: Arguin-Creighton 2026, Thm 1.1 (unconditional): for alpha > 0 and V ~ alpha log log T, (1/T) meas{t in [0,T] : log|zeta(1/2+it)| > V} >= K_alpha times a Gaussian tail with variance (1/2) log log T, with K_alpha >> (C alpha^2 log alpha)^{-alpha^2} as alpha -> infinity. This recovers the sharpest unconditional lower bounds for fractional moments (Heap-Soundararajan). Arguin-Bailey-Roberts 2026, Thm 1.1 (RH): for k > 0 and V ~ k log log T, (1/T) meas{t in [T,2T] : log|zeta(1/2+it)| > V} <= C_k e^{-V^2/log log T}/sqrt(log log T), with C_k = exp(e^{ck}); this recovers Harper's moment bound. The matching unconditional upper bound for 0 < alpha < 2 is due to Arguin-Bailey 2023.
value: Gaussian-order decay up to constants across the whole regime V of order log log T (lower bound unconditional; upper bound unconditional for alpha < 2 and conditional on RH for all alpha)
conditional_on: Lower bound: none. Upper bound for alpha >= 2: RH (Arguin-Bailey-Roberts).
location: AC26 Theorem 1.1 and Corollary 1.2, p.2; ABR26 (arXiv 2604.25579) Theorem 1.1 and Corollary 1.2, p.1-2

quantity: Other L-functions, t-aspect: GL(2) Weyl barrier (distinct from classical zeta)
statement: For a fixed SL(2,Z) Hecke cusp form f, L(1/2+it,f) << t^{1/3+eps} (Good 1982, Weyl strength; extended by Meurman and Jutila). As of 2026-11-17 no sub-Weyl t-aspect bound for any GL(2) L-function is established; classical zeta is the only case where a sub-Weyl bound is known. Holowinsky-Munshi-Sharma-Streipel (arXiv 2503.00656 v1, Mar 2025) claimed L(1/2+it,f) << t^{1/3-1/174+eps} (which would also give zeta << t^{1/6-1/348+eps}). That paper was WITHDRAWN on 2026-10-09 (v2): 'An error has been identified in the section 6 of the current version where a certain degeneracy occurs. The authors are working to address it.'
value: Established: 1/3 (Weyl); withdrawn claim: 1/3 - 1/174
conditional_on: none
location: HMSS v1, introduction p.1 ('Good's bound has so far remained unsurpassed...'), Theorem 1, p.2; arXiv abs page, v2 withdrawal comment dated 9 Oct 2026

history.note: HMSS 2025 does not count it ('remained unsurpassed'); its status is unclear and it is not counted here

caveats: Do not transfer zeta's 13/84 to other L-functions. Good's bound is cited here via HMSS's introduction (secondary for Good's original). This entry records a negative status event (a withdrawal), not a new bound.

The arXiv abs page fetched 2026-11-17 reads 'This paper has been withdrawn by Prahlad Sharma', v2 dated 9 Oct 2026, with the comment about a degeneracy in §6; the latest version has no PDF. verification.correction: Remove or qualify 'classical zeta is the only case where a sub-Weyl bound is known'. HMSS's intro says so, but their own abstract says 'beyond GL(1)'. Sub-Weyl bounds are known in GL(1) beyond zeta. In the t-aspect, Dirichlet L(1/2+it,chi) with fixed chi follows via Hurwitz-zeta sums of (a+mq)^{-it}, to which the same exponent-pair and Bombieri-Iwaniec machinery applies. In the depth aspect, Milićević 2016 proves sub-Weyl bounds for prime-power moduli. The correct statement: no sub-Weyl bound beyond GL(1) is established. Good's venue is confirmed: Mathematika 29 (1982) 278-295.
verification.notes: The withdrawal event and its date are confirmed. If the HMSS route were repaired it would give only 1/6-1/348 ≈ 0.16379 for zeta, worse than 13/84.

quantity: Explicit standard zero-free region constant R for Dirichlet L-functions, region Re s >= 1 - 1/(R log(q max(1,|t|)))
statement: Kadiri, Theorem 1.1: for 3 <= q <= 400 000 and every non-principal primitive chi mod q, L(s,chi) has no zero in Re s >= 1 - 1/(5.60 log(q max(1,|Im s|))). The proof uses Platt's partial GRH verification (LFUN-12) as an input. For general q, the best published explicit constant is McCurley's (quoted as Kadiri Theorem 2.2). With M = max{q, q|Im s|, 10} and R = 9.645908801, the product of the phi(q) L-functions mod q has at most one zero in Re s >= 1 - 1/(R log M), and such a zero is a simple real zero of a real character. Large-|t| regime: Khale (arXiv 2210.06457, Thm 1.1) gives an explicit Vinogradov-Korobov region, L(s,chi) != 0 for sigma >= 1 - 1/(10.5 log q + 61.5 (log|t|)^{2/3}(log log|t|)^{1/3}), |t| >= 10.
value: R = 5.60 (3 <= q <= 4*10^5, no exceptions); R = 9.645908801 (all q, one possible exceptional real zero)
location: Kadiri arXiv v2 p.1, Theorem 1.1 (eq. 1.1). McCurley's constant: Kadiri Theorem 2.2, citing McCurley, J. Number Theory 19 (1984), Theorem 1. Khale: arXiv 2210.06457v1, Theorem 1.1, eqs. (1.2)-(1.3).

caveats: Kadiri 2018 promised a follow-up for q > 400 000. In Oct 2026, Lu-Zaman-Zhao (arXiv 2602.03626v2, p.1) still cite only McCurley's c = 1/10 for general q, so no published general-q improvement was found. Khale's footnote says the paper depends on Ford's zeta computations, which were later reissued 'with minor numerical corrections'; this is an upstream erratum. Classical zeta has its own, separate explicit records (e.g. Bellotti-Trudgian-Yang 2603.21490: 1/(4.896 log t), unrefereed); they do not transfer to L(s,chi). quantity: Zero-free half-plane Re s > theta (theta < 1) for all Dirichlet L-functions (quasi-GRH / QRH)
statement: OpenAI, 'The Quasi-Riemann Hypothesis' (5 Oct 2026, human-assisted), Theorem 1.1: every finite-order Hecke L-function over K = Q(sqrt(-3)) has no zeros in Re s > 11/12. Hence every Dirichlet L-function, including zeta(s), is zero-free there. Corollary 1.2 states sup_{q<=x,(a,q)=1} |pi(x;q,a) - Li(x)/phi(q)| << x^{11/12} log x with absolute, effective constants. The paper also asserts h(D) >> sqrt|D|/log log|D| effectively, Vinogradov's least-nonresidue conjecture, and that Euler's list of 65 idoneal numbers is complete. A companion manuscript (30 Sep 2026; Lean formalization claimed) asserts the half-plane Re s > 7/8. Unrefereed follow-ups claim about 0.8749 for Hecke L-functions over every number field (B. Liu, arXiv 2610.26835). Cureton-Thorner (with AxiomProver) claim Re s > 31/32 for all Dedekind zeta functions (Hexagon preprint 2610.00200v2, cited by Banks 2610.31402).

quantity: Siegel's ineffective lower bound for L(1,chi) and Tatuzawa's effective version with one exception
statement: Siegel (1935): for every eps > 0 there is an ineffective c3(eps) > 0 with L(1,chi) >= c3(eps) q^{-eps} for all primitive quadratic chi mod q. Harcos-Thorner report that Tatuzawa's Theorem 1 permits c4 = eps/10. This is equivalent to an effective Siegel-type zero-free interval sigma >= 1 - c5(eps) q^{-eps} for all but one character.

quantity: Uniform exclusion of Landau-Siegel zeros: an absolute c with (1-beta) log q >= c for every real zero beta of every primitive real L(s,chi), q >= 3
statement: OpenAI, Theorem 1 (manuscript dated 1 Oct 2026): there is an absolute c > 0 such that every real zero beta in (0,1) of every primitive nonprincipal real Dirichlet L-function of conductor q >= 3 satisfies (1-beta) log q >= c. The method is an interpolation determinant in Q(sqrt d, sqrt 2). Its only analytic input is the prime bias forced by a real zero: Sum_{p<=X, chi(p)=1} log p / p << log q + (1-beta)(log X)^2. Independent human expositions: Banks (2610.15483, Thm 1.1) gives q0 = 10^10 and delta0 = 3.0*10^-3, hence c = 3.0*10^-3 for all q >= 3 using LFUN-08. Guo (2610.30476, Thm 1.1) gives an elementary proof with c = 1/100 for every q >= 3. Kerr (2610.21099) gives a simpler proof that replaces the determinant with pigeonhole plus Masser's zero estimate. Kimura (2610.21511, Thm 1) gives (1-beta) log q >= 5811*10^-7 for all q >= 3, checked in Lean. Banks (2610.31402) extends the result to quadratic characters over any base field k with an effective c(k) and derives an effective Brauer-Siegel theorem for Galois extensions of k.
value: c = 1/100 (Guo, elementary); c = 3.0*10^-3 (Banks; uses LZZ for q < 10^10); c = 5.811*10^-4 (Kimura, Lean-checked)

Evidence for correctness is strong but informal: there are at least four independent human write-ups (Banks, Kerr, Guo, Green's Hexagon preprint 2610.00311v2, which reports 'arguments all due to ChatGPT'), and Kimura's Lean proof was checked by the Lean kernel and an independent kernel. Kimura states that his Theorems 1 and 10 'do not depend on the correctness of the text of [SZ]'. The Observatory compiled none of this Lean code. Quanta (2026-11-05, fetched) reports no errors and quotes Granville ('It's all moot now'). Tao reportedly wrote that 'the Siegel zero problem has been solved in a number of ways' (Observatory secondary note). No dispute was found in searches on 2026-11-17. The different constants (1/100, 3e-3, 5.8e-4) are all lower bounds proved by different routes, so they do not conflict. Scope: the result excludes Siegel zeros in the asymptotic sense, i.e. (1-beta) log q -> 0 is impossible. It does not prove the standard region with McCurley's c = 1/10 for all q, which is known computationally only for q <= 10^10 (LFUN-08). It says nothing about complex zeros near Re s = 1/2.

quantity: Log-free zero-density estimates for Dirichlet L-functions near sigma = 1 (explicit and asymptotic exponents)
statement: Thorner-Zaman, Theorem 1.2: let N(sigma,Q) count zeros with beta > sigma and |gamma| <= Q of the product of L(s,chi) over primitive chi mod q, q <= Q, and let N* exclude the largest real zero beta1(Q). For Q >= 3 and sigma >= 39/40: N(sigma,Q) <= 10^88 (10^421 Q^99)^{1-sigma}, and N*(sigma,Q) <= 10^93 min{1,(1-beta1(Q)) log Q} (10^466 Q^170)^{1-sigma}. These are the first fully explicit log-free density estimates. Asymptotically, Jutila gives N(sigma,Q) <= c(eps) Q^{(6+eps)(1-sigma)} for sigma >= 4/5, which matches what the generalized Lindelof hypothesis gives. Single-modulus hybrid density: Huxley gives exponent 12/5. Chen-Gupta-Li (arXiv 2507.08296, unrefereed) claim Sum_{chi mod q} N(sigma,T,chi) <<_eps (qT)^{7(1-sigma)/3+eps}, adapting Guth-Maynard.
value: explicit exponents 99 / 170 (Q-aspect, sigma >= 39/40); asymptotic 6+eps (Jutila); hybrid single-modulus 12/5 (Huxley) -> 7/3 (claimed)
location: arXiv 2208.11123v4 p.2, Theorem 1.2; eqs. (1.3)-(1.5) for Gallagher, Jutila, Bombieri. Chen-Gupta-Li: arXiv 2507.08296 abstract.

history.value: numerically sharp asymptotic log-free density near sigma = 1 (feeds Linnik)

caveats: The explicit constants are enormous (10^421) and are useful only through their shape. Thorner-Zaman note that improving them would not much help their application without a numerical improvement in the standard zero-free region. Chen-Gupta-Li is unrefereed. The abstract I read does not say whether the q^{eps} loss allows log-free use near sigma = 1.

quantity: Rigorous numerical verification of GRH for Dirichlet L-functions: moduli range and height
statement: Platt, Theorem 7.1: GRH holds for Dirichlet L-functions of primitive characters with modulus q <= 400 000, up to height t0 = max(10^8/q, 7.5*10^7/q + 200) for even q and t0 = max(10^8/q, 3.75*10^7/q + 200) for odd q. This covers 29 565 923 837 L-functions and about 3.8*10^13 zeros, used about 400 000 core hours, and relies on interval arithmetic and rigorous up-sampling. Theorem 7.2: L(1/2,chi) != 0 for every primitive chi with q <= 2 000 000.
value: q <= 4*10^5, height about 10^8/q (at least 200); central non-vanishing q <= 2*10^6
location: arXiv 1305.3087v1, Sec. 7 (p.14-15), Theorems 7.1 and 7.2

history.value: q <= 13 to height 10 000; other moduli to 2 500; largest q = 432; about 10^7 zeros

caveats: This is finite evidence. The 2018 Kadiri paper and the 2026 Lu-Zaman-Zhao paper both still cite Platt 2016 as the GRH benchmark, and no larger all-character verification was found. Rigor depends on interval arithmetic and Turing-method bookkeeping; I did not replay any part. Classical zeta verification is a separate record and is not covered here. A height of about 10^8/q is small for large q, so this is a box verification, not a verification of GRH in the q-aspect.

quantity: Degree classification of the Selberg class (d < 2)
statement: The (extended) Selberg class S# has no elements with 0 < d < 1 (Conrey-Ghosh 1993; Kaczorowski-Perelli 1999). For d = 1, the elements of S are the Riemann zeta function and shifts L(s+i theta, chi) of primitive Dirichlet L-functions (Kaczorowski-Perelli, Acta Math. 182 (1999)). S#_d is empty for 1 < d < 2 (Kaczorowski-Perelli, 'On the structure of the Selberg class VII: 1 < d < 2', Ann. of Math. 173 (2011) 1397-1441). Balasubramanian-Raghunathan, Theorem 1.1, extend the last result to a much larger class A# (no absolute-convergence or Ramanujan-type requirements; contains tensor, exterior and symmetric square L-functions): A#_d is empty for 1 < d < 2, with a shorter proof. For degree 2 and conductor 1, Kaczorowski-Perelli (arXiv 2009.12329) classify S# through an invariant chi_F.
value: no degrees in (0,1) or (1,2); d = 1 fully classified; d = 2 classified only for conductor 1
location: Balasubramanian-Raghunathan arXiv 2011.07525v1 p.2 Theorem 1.1 and Conjecture 2.5; refs [CG93], [KP99], [KP11] on p.15-16. KP 2009.12329 abstract.

history.value: degree 2 conductor 1 classification; invariants of degree-2 L-functions (2405.03186, 2611.21046)

caveats: The degree conjecture (no non-integer degrees) is open for d > 2. Classification of degree 2 in general is open. Membership of all degree-2 elements as automorphic L-functions is proved only for conductor 1. I read the Kaczorowski-Perelli Annals and Acta results only through the statements and references in Balasubramanian-Raghunathan.

quantity: Davenport-Heilbronn function: count of off-line zeros (qualitative theorem)
statement: The Davenport-Heilbronn function f(s) = 5^{-s}[zeta(s,1/5) + k zeta(s,2/5) - k zeta(s,3/5) - zeta(s,4/5)], with k = (sqrt(10-2 sqrt 5) - 2)/(sqrt 5 - 1), has period-5 coefficients and a Riemann-type functional equation, but no Euler product. Its zeros satisfy N_L(sigma1,sigma2,T) asymptotic to T for every 1/2 < sigma1 < sigma2 <= a_L, so a positive density of zeros lies off the critical line, including zeros in sigma > 1 (Davenport-Heilbronn 1936). The number of zeros on the critical line is >> T (Voronin); Karatsuba gives Omega >> (log T)^{1/2-eps}; Selberg (late 1990s) shows a positive proportion of zeros lies on the line.
value: N(sigma1,sigma2,T) asymptotic to T off-line; positive proportion on-line
location: arXiv 2411.18492v1 Sec. 1, pp.1-2 (N_L estimates, Voronin, Karatsuba (1), Selberg)

history.value: many zeros on the line, positive density off it

caveats: This is the key negative result for the area: a Riemann-type functional equation plus Dirichlet-series analyticity does not imply RH. Any proof of GRH must use the Euler product. Primary sources were not opened; the statements come from Rezvyakova's introduction.

verification.checked_against: Rezvyakova arXiv 2411.18492v1 Sec 1, pp.1-3: N_L(T) ≍ T log T; N_L(sigma1,sigma2,T) ≍ T for 1/2 < sigma1 < sigma2 <= a_L; N0(g,T) >> T 'following the ideas of [9]'; Voronin's Omega_g >> exp((1/20) sqrt(log log log log T)); Karatsuba (log T)^{1/2-eps}; Selberg (late 90s) positive proportion. Bombieri-Hejhal conditional almost-all. Primary 1936 paper not opened.
verification.correction: (1) The off-line count is N_L(sigma1,sigma2,T) ≍ T (order of magnitude), not 'asymptotic to T'. (2) Since N_L(T) ≍ T log T, the off-line zeros form a density-zero subset of all zeros, so 'a positive density of zeros lies off the critical line' is wrong. They are infinitely many, ≫ T up to height T, and the conjecture (proved conditionally by Bombieri-Hejhal for Epstein) is that almost all zeros lie on the line. (3) 'Zeros on the line >> T' comes from Hardy-Littlewood-type ideas per Rezvyakova. Voronin's contribution is that N0(g,T)/T tends to infinity. The same error about positive density is repeated in frontier negative result 1.
verification.notes: The conclusion that the Euler product is essential stands.

quantity: Epstein zeta functions of binary positive definite forms: off-line zeros vs zeros on the critical line
statement: For binary positive definite quadratic forms (class number > 1), the Epstein zeta function is a linear combination of degree-2 Hecke L-functions. It has a Riemann-type functional equation but no Euler product, and has many zeros off the critical line, including zeros in sigma > 1 (Davenport-Heilbronn 1936). Bombieri-Hejhal show, conditionally on GRH and Montgomery-type pair correlation for Hecke L-functions, that almost all zeros lie on the line. Rezvyakova (2024) proves unconditionally that a positive proportion of nontrivial zeros of the Epstein zeta function of any binary positive definite form with integer coefficients lies on the critical line.
value: positive proportion on the line (unconditional, claimed 2024); almost all on the line (conditional on GRH + pair correlation)
location: arXiv 2411.18492v1 abstract and Sec. 1 pp.1-2 (Bombieri-Hejhal refs [2],[3]; off-line zeros refs [5],[41])

quantity: Function-field Riemann hypothesis
statement: Weil (1948) proved RH for zeta functions of smooth projective curves over finite fields: all zeros have Re s = 1/2, i.e. Frobenius eigenvalues of absolute value q^{1/2}. Deligne (1974, Weil I) proved RH for smooth projective varieties: eigenvalues on H^i have absolute value q^{i/2}. Elementary proofs for curves were later given by Stepanov and Bombieri.
value: RH proved (curves 1948; all smooth projective varieties 1974)
location: Standard; survey: J. Milne, arXiv 1509.00797 (not opened here)
caveats: The decisive ingredients are a positivity property (Castelnuovo-Severi / Hodge index for curves) and cohomological Frobenius. The number-field analogue lacks both, which is the standard structural explanation of why no transfer exists. The OpenAI release also contains a 'function-field generic Ramanujan' manuscript (unrefereed; not read).

quantity: Ihara zeta RH / Ramanujan graphs: existence of d-regular Ramanujan graphs (max nontrivial |lambda| <= 2 sqrt(d-1))
statement: For a d-regular graph, the Ihara zeta function satisfies the graph RH exactly when the graph is Ramanujan. Huang-McKenzie-Yau, Theorem 1.2 and Corollary 1.3: fix d >= 3. With the normalized adjacency eigenvalues lambda_2 and -lambda_N of a uniformly random simple d-regular graph on N vertices, both converge to Tracy-Widom_1 (GOE edge universality). As a consequence, for N sufficiently large, a random d-regular graph is Ramanujan (max{lambda_2, |lambda_N|} <= 2 in the normalization A/sqrt(d-1)) with probability approximately 69%. This yields infinite families of non-bipartite Ramanujan graphs for every degree d >= 3. Marcus-Spielman-Srivastava had settled the bipartite case for all degrees.
value: about 69% of random d-regular graphs are Ramanujan (every fixed d >= 3)
location: arXiv 2412.20263v2 abstract; Sec. 1, Theorem 1.2 and Corollary 1.3 (p.~7); background p.~3

quantity: Selberg zeta RH / small Laplace eigenvalues: lower bounds for lambda1 (congruence surfaces) and typical spectral gaps
statement: For a finite-area hyperbolic surface, zeros of the Selberg zeta function off Re s = 1/2 (in (1/2,1)) correspond exactly to small eigenvalues 0 < lambda < 1/4. So the Selberg-zeta RH is equivalent to lambda1 >= 1/4 (Monk, Remark 1.2: Selberg's 1/4 conjecture is 'the analogue of the Riemann hypothesis for the Selberg zeta function'). Congruence surfaces: Selberg (1965) proved lambda1 >= 3/16. Kim-Sarnak (2003, appendix to Kim, JAMS) proved lambda1 >= (1/4)(1 - 49/1024) = 975/4096, about 0.2380 (exponent theta = 7/64). Random surfaces: Hide-Magee (Ann. of Math. 198 (2023)) show random degree-n covers of a finite-area non-compact surface have no new eigenvalues below 1/4 - eps whp, giving closed surfaces with genus -> infinity and lambda1 -> 1/4. Anantharaman-Monk: Weil-Petersson-random genus-g surfaces have lambda1 >= 1/4 - eps with probability -> 1 (Monk, Theorem 1.1; full proof in arXiv 2502.12268).
value: congruence: lambda1 >= 975/4096; random/typical: lambda1 >= 1/4 - eps
location: Monk arXiv 2601.15157v1 p.3-5, Theorem 1.1, Table 1, Remark 1.2 (quotes Kim-Sarnak bound and Selberg 3/16); Hide-Magee arXiv 2107.05292 abstract; zbMATH 1018.11024 (Kim, with appendix by Kim-Sarnak)
caveats: Monk stresses that congruence surfaces are a countable, measure-zero set, so random-surface results imply nothing for the Selberg 1/4 conjecture. Compact surfaces can have small eigenvalues, so RH fails for general Selberg zeta functions and arithmeticity is essential. The Anantharaman-Monk 1/4 - eps result is a preprint (refereeing status not verified). Nothing improving 7/64 for congruence subgroups over Q was found.

quantity: Exponent θ in E(T) ≪ T^{θ+ε}: the error term in the second moment (k=1)
statement: Unconditional. With E(T) defined by ∫_0^T |ζ(1/2+it)|^2 dt = T log(T/2π) + (2γ−1)T + E(T), Bourgain–Watt prove E(T) = O(T^{1515/4816+ε}) for every ε>0, where 1515/4816 = 0.314576... This improves Watt's E(T) = O(T^{131/416}(log T)^{32587/8320}), with 131/416 = 0.314903...
location: Theorem 4 and the remark after it, p.1 of arXiv v1. The obstruction to going further is discussed in §6, remark (iii), p.16.

The arXiv v2 comment (July 2023) reports a gap in Propositions 2, 3 and 1′ and says 'Theorems 1, 2 and 3 lose their status as theorems.' This replaces Motohashi's C_1 = 8 and C_2 = 22.
value: E_2(T) ≪ T^{2/3}(log T)^{10/3} (preprint). The power 2/3 is refereed (Ivić–Motohashi 1995). Conjectured E_2(T) ≪ T^{1/2+ε}.

quantity: Power exponent e in ∫_0^T |ζ(1/2+it)|^6 dt ≪ T^{e+ε} (sixth moment, k=3)
statement: de Faveri–Pandey (unrefereed, Oct 2026), Theorem 1.1: for every T ≥ 1 and ε > 0, ∫_0^T |ζ(1/2+it)|^6 dt ≪_ε T^{5/4 − 1/60 + ε} = T^{37/30+ε}. The best refereed bound is T^{5/4+ε}. It comes from interpolating Hardy–Littlewood/Ingham's M_4 ≪ T^{1+ε} with Heath-Brown's M_12 ≪ T^{2+ε} (1978), which gives M_k ≪ T^{1+(k−4)/8+ε} for 4 ≤ k ≤ 12 (k = power).
value: e ≤ 37/30 ≈ 1.2333 (preprint). Refereed: e ≤ 5/4. Conjectured: I_3(T) ~ 42 a_3 T(log T)^9/9!, i.e. e = 1.

caveats: (1) Unrefereed and only six weeks old as of 2026-11-17. (2) The authors disclose AI use (p.3–4): 'ChatGPT 6 Astra' autonomously produced a simpler argument extending the admissible η-range in the key large-value estimate to |η| = o(W/N^2), and a refinement of that argument is used in the paper. This step needs independent human verification. (3) Iwaniec (Funct. Approx. 71 (2024) 121–125) noted that M_6 ≪ T^{6/5−δ} would beat Huxley's zero-density bound at σ = 3/4. Since 37/30 > 6/5, the new bound does not reach that threshold (Guth–Maynard, Ann. Math. 2026, improved zero density by other means). (4) Conflicting claim: Altenschmidt claims M_6 ≪ T^{1+ε} (MOM-06). It is not recognized by this paper or by the Florea survey. (5) The GL3 analogue is not classical ζ: the second moment of a GL3 L-function is known only up to T^{4/3+ε} (Dasgupta–Leung–Young), as cited on p.2.

quantity: Large values of |ζ(1/2+it)| at the critical level V ≈ T^{1/8}
statement: Let N(T,V) be the size of the largest 1-spaced subset of {t ∈ [T,2T] : |ζ(1/2+it)| ≥ V}. The classical moment bounds give N(T,V) ≪ T^ε min(T V^{−4}, T^2 V^{−12}), with the two bounds crossing at V = T^{1/8}. de Faveri–Pandey, Theorem 1.3: for V ∈ [T^{7/60}, T^{5/38}], N(T,V) ≪_ε T^{24/17+ε} V^{−128/17}. At V = T^{1/8} this gives T^{8/17+ε} instead of T^{1/2+ε}, the first improvement since Hardy–Littlewood (1923) on the measure of the set where |ζ| ≥ T^{1/8}. The underlying Corollary 1.4 covers D_η(w) = Σ_{N<n≤2N} a_n e(w φ_η(n/N)) with φ_η(x) = √x + ηx^{3/2}, |a_n| ≤ 1, N ≤ W ≤ N^{4/3} and |η| ≤ cW/N^2. For 1-spaced W ⊂ [0,W] with |D_η| ≥ V it gives |W| ≪ N^ε(N^2/V^2 + N^{3/2}W^{3/4}Υ^{1/8}/V^3 + N^{5/2}W^{3/2}Υ^{1/4}/V^5), where Υ = 1 + |η|W.
location: Eq. (2) and Theorem 1.3, p.2. Corollary 1.4, p.2. Further N(T,V) bounds in §9 (Theorem 9.1).

history.note: trace method with third powers, as in Guth–Maynard

caveats: Negative result recorded in the same paper (§1.2, p.3). With ℓ^2-bounded coefficients the mean-value bound |W| ≪ W/√N is sharp when η = 0 (a_n = N^{1/4}·1_square(n); counterexample of Guth/Cohen/Fu–Guth–Maldague). An ℓ^∞ hypothesis is therefore essential. The generic large-sieve and Halász–Montgomery bounds meet at V ≍ N^{3/4}, the same critical regime as in Guth–Maynard. For V > T^{1/8} better bounds already followed from exponent pairs (Trudgian–Yang 2025).

quantity: Conditional asymptotics for the sixth and eighth moments
statement: Ng: a conjectural formula, with power savings, for a family of ternary additive divisor sums (correlations of d_3) implies an asymptotic formula with power-saving error for ∫|ζ(1/2+it)|^6. This makes the Conrey–Gonek heuristic rigorous under that hypothesis and improves Ivić's conditional upper bound. Ng–Shen–Wong: RH together with a quaternary additive divisor conjecture implies an asymptotic formula for the eighth moment. A key input is a sharp RH-conditional bound for a shifted moment.
value: k = 3 and k = 4 asymptotics, conditional only
conditional_on: Ng: ternary additive divisor conjecture with power savings. Ng–Shen–Wong: RH + quaternary additive divisor conjecture.
location: Main theorem as described in the abstract. Ng–Shen–Wong arXiv:2204.13891, abstract.

history.value: conditional upper bound for the sixth moment from a d_3 correlation conjecture
conditional eighth-moment asymptotic (RH + quaternary divisor conjecture)

caveats: The hypotheses (uniform power-saving asymptotics for Σ d_3(n)d_3(n+h), and its quaternary analogue) are open. de Faveri–Pandey (p.2) describe the unconditional sixth-moment problem as essentially needing a remainder better than X^{7/6} for Σ_{h∼X^{1/3}} Σ_{n∼X} d_3(n)d_3(n+h). Other L-functions, not classical ζ: Conrey–Iwaniec–Soundararajan (arXiv 0710.5176) proved a sixth-moment asymptotic for Dirichlet L-functions with an extra average over moduli and t. Results like this do not transfer to ζ.

quantity: Admissible length θ in the twisted second moment ∫|ζ(1/2+it)A(1/2+it)|^2 φ(t/T) dt with arbitrary coefficients a_n ≪ n^ε, A of length T^θ
statement: Bettin–Chandee–Radziwiłł, Theorem 1: if θ < 1/2 + δ with δ = 1/66, i.e. θ < 17/33 = 0.5151..., then I = Σ_{d,e ≤ T^θ} (a_d \bar a_e/[d,e]) ∫ (log(t(d,e)^2/(2πde)) + 2γ) φ(t/T) dt + O(T^{3/20+ε}N^{33/20} + T^{1/3+ε}) with N = T^θ. Off-diagonal terms contribute to the main term. Using Duke–Friedlander–Iwaniec instead of the Bettin–Chandee trilinear bound gives δ = 1/190.
value: θ < 17/33 for arbitrary coefficients. For structured coefficients: θ < 9/17 for mollifiers (BCHB) and 4/7 (Conrey 1989, mollifier-type, from memory).
location: Theorem 1, p.2. Discussion of the θ = 1 conjecture, p.2. Theorem 2 and Corollary 1 (conditional on trilinear Conjecture 1 ⇒ Lindelöf), p.3. Theorem 3 (products, θ < 1/2+1/10) and Theorem 4 (A·B with smooth A of length T^{1/2}, θ < 3/4), pp.4–5.
caveats: Erratum and withdrawal. Dong–Robles–Zeindler, 'Bilinear forms with Kloosterman fractions and applications' (arXiv:2601.00292, Jan 2026), claimed δ = 1/46. The v2 comment (5 Jan 2026) says: 'We accidentally missed a factor of L^2 in equation (2.53), which turns L^5 into L^7. The rest of the argument is still valid, but does not lead to an improved bound as claimed', and credits A. Pascadi with finding the error. The PDF is no longer served. 17/33 therefore stands. Negative results from BCR p.2: the formula fails in general for θ > 1, and the 'θ = 1 conjecture' for θ < 1 would imply Lindelöf. Recent reciprocity formulas (Khan arXiv 2401.01057; Tang arXiv 2608.14852) were seen in abstract only.

Going further 'without including new ingredients specific to ζ(s)' seems unlikely. quantity: Unconditional spectral realization of the critical zeros of Hecke L-functions on the adele class space (Connes, Sobolev parameter delta)
statement: Let k be a global field, chi a character of C_{k,1} and delta > 1. Let D_chi be the generator of the scaling (idele class) action on the cokernel H_chi inside L^2_delta. Then D_chi has discrete spectrum, and Sp D_chi is contained in iR. Precisely, rho is in Sp D_chi iff L(chi~, 1/2 + rho) = 0 and rho is in iR. So the spectrum is the set of imaginary parts of the zeros that already lie ON the critical line. The multiplicity is the largest integer n < (1+delta)/2 with n <= the multiplicity of the zero. Corollary 2: for h in S(C_k), W(h) is trace class and Trace W(h) = sum of h^(chi~, rho) over critical zeros rho in iR/N-perp. The zeta case is k = Q, chi = 1.
value: Sp D_chi = {rho in iR : L(chi~,1/2+rho)=0}; multiplicity = min(m_rho, max{n : n < (1+delta)/2})
location: Section III, Theorem 1 (p. 13 of arXiv v1) and Corollary 2 (p. 14); proof in Appendix I

history.value: announcement of the delta-Sobolev spectral realization (C. R. Acad. Sci. Paris note)
history.note: memory_unverified; cited as [Co] in the 1999 paper

history.value: Theorem 1 as stated (delta > 1, critical zeros only)
delta removed: canonical Hilbert space L^2 of a circle (zeta-cycles); see LED-OPS-4

caveats: Only zeros already on the critical line appear. Off-line zeros are invisible as an 'absorption spectrum', so the theorem has no RH content and is in this sense tautological. The Sobolev weight delta is ad hoc, and the multiplicity depends on delta. Connes says himself that the result is only 'preliminary' because of delta (p. 2). No erratum found.

verification.checked_against: arXiv math/9811068v1 full text: Theorem 1 (p.13), Corollary 2 (p.14), intro pp.2-3 ('only preliminary because it requires the use of an unnatural parameter δ'); reference [Co] = C. R. Acad. Sci. Paris 1996

quantity: Connes trace formula: S-local trace formula (proved) versus global trace formula (equivalent to RH for all Hecke L-functions)
statement: Theorem 4 (unconditional): for a finite set S of places and compactly supported h in S(C_S), as Lambda -> infinity, Trace(R_Lambda U(h)) = 2h(1) log' Lambda + sum over v in S of the principal value integral of h(u^{-1})/|1-u| d*u over k_v*, + o(1). Theorem 5: for a global field k of POSITIVE characteristic, with Q_Lambda the projection onto the span of f in S(A) such that f and f^ vanish for |x| > Lambda, the global analogue of this formula holds for every compactly supported h iff all Hecke L-functions on k satisfy RH. The direction a) => b) goes through positivity of the Weil distribution. For number fields (k = Q) the paper only indicates the analogue: the archimedean cutoff is handled by Landau–Pollak–Slepian prolate theory, and the paper says 'This gives the analogue of Lemma 1, Theorem 5, and Lemma 3' (p. 47) without a detailed proof. The RH-equivalent gap is the global (all places) trace formula.
value: S-local formula: proved for every finite S. Global formula <=> RH(all Grössencharakter L-functions): proved in characteristic p, sketched for Q
location: Section VII Theorem 4 (p. 31); Section VIII Theorem 5 (p. 43), Lemma 3 (p. 44); number-field remarks pp. 45-47 (prolate operator, eq. (32)); semiclassical count eq. (43)

history.value: S-local trace formula; equivalence proved in characteristic p only
rigorous virtual representation whose character is the Weil distribution (all zeros); see LED-OPS-3
semilocal trace formula used to write QW_lambda as a trace (Andrews–Connes–La Gatta 2026, Theorem 8.1)

caveats: In characteristic p, RH is Weil's theorem, so Theorem 5 adds no new RH case. For Q the equivalence is a sketch, not a proved theorem in this paper. Do not cite this paper as proving 'global trace formula <=> RH' for zeta. The abstract's wording ('reduces the Riemann hypothesis to the validity of the trace formula') is accurate only in this sense.

quantity: Spectral interpretation of ALL zeros and poles (virtual representation of the idele class group)
statement: For any global field K there is a virtual representation of the idele class group, built from natural function spaces on the adeles and idele classes, whose character equals the Weil distribution in Weil's explicit formula. It is a spectral interpretation of all zeros (on or off the line) and poles of the L-functions. The construction uses nuclear (non-Hilbert) function spaces, so no self-adjointness or positivity follows.
value: spectral realization of all zeros (with multiplicity) and poles: unconditional; gives no RH
location: Abstract (main theorem); full text not opened

history.value: all zeros, as a virtual representation

caveats: This shows that a spectral realization by itself carries no information about RH. The RH content of any Hilbert–Pólya construction lies entirely in a Hilbert-space positivity or self-adjointness statement, and every such statement found in this survey is equivalent to Weil positivity.

source.title: On a representation of the idele class group related to primes and zeros of L-functions

verification.checked_against: arXiv math/0311468v3 abstract and Introduction pp.1-3; Crossref 10.1215/s0012-7094-04-12734-4 (Duke 127(3) 519-595, 2005)
verification.correction: The character equals 'a variant of the Weil distribution' (Meyer's abstract), not the Weil distribution itself. Meyer also says the representation CAN be moved to a Banach or Hilbert space but cannot be made UNITARY once there are multiple or off-line zeros. So the obstruction is unitarity, not the impossibility of a Hilbert space. Meyer also notes that positivity of the modified Weil distribution is equivalent to GRH. The results are stated mainly for number fields, 'with small modifications' for function fields.
verification.notes: Venue and pages are confirmed. Evidence upgraded: the introduction was read, not only the abstract.

quantity: Zeta-cycles: realization of critical zeros on the canonical L^2 of a circle (removes Connes' delta)
statement: Let C = R*_+/mu^Z be a circle of length L = log mu, and Sigma_mu E : S_0^ev -> L^2(C) the scale-invariant Riemann-sum map, where E(f)(u) = u^{1/2} sum_{n>=1} f(nu). C is a zeta-cycle if Sigma_mu E(S_0^ev) is not dense in L^2(C). Theorem 1.1: (i) the spectrum of R*_+ on the orthogonal complement of Sigma_mu E(S_0^ev) in L^2(C) consists of imaginary parts of zeros of zeta on the critical line. (ii) If zeta(1/2 + is) = 0 with s > 0, then every circle whose length is an integer multiple of 2 pi/s is a zeta-cycle, and its spectrum contains s. Numerically, the low-lying spectrum of perturbed spectral triples reproduces the first 31 zeros.
value: spectrum on (Sigma_mu E)^perp is contained in {critical-zero ordinates}; every critical zero is realized on circles of length in (2 pi/s)Z_{>0}
location: Definition 1.1 and Theorem 1.1 (p. 4); Theorem 6.4 (Section 6)

history.value: canonical L^2(C); also found very small eigenvalues of the Weil form on a window, with eigenvectors given by prolate functions

caveats: As with LED-OPS-1, only critical zeros are seen, so the theorem has no RH content. The 31-zero agreement is a numerical observation, not a theorem.

quantity: Weil positivity at the archimedean place: largest support window on which positivity is proved, and the Sonin-trace inequality (classical zeta)
statement: Theorem 1: let g in C_c^inf(R*_+) have support in [2^{-1/2}, 2^{1/2}] and Fourier transform vanishing at i/2 and 0. Then W_inf(g * g^*) >= Tr(theta(g) S theta(g)^*), where S is the orthogonal projection of L^2(R)^ev onto the Sonin space (even functions that, together with their Fourier transform, vanish on [-1,1]). Theorem 6.11: dropping the condition at 0, W_inf(g*g^*) >= Tr(theta(g) S theta(g)^*) - c|g^(0)|^2 with a finite constant 13 < c < 17. Corollary 2: c|g^(0)|^2 + sum over zeros s of g^(s) conj(g^(s)) >= Tr(theta(g) S theta(g)^*). The earlier, weaker statement is due to Yoshida: W_inf(f) >= 0 for every smooth positive-definite f supported in (1/2, 2) with f^(+-i/2) = 0.
value: support window: f = g*g^* in (1/2, 2), i.e. lambda^2 = 2; Sonin inequality with constant c in (13, 17)
location: Introduction, Theorem 1 and Corollary 2 (pp. 2-3); Theorem 6.11 (p. 48, eq. (141)); computer-assisted Facts 6.1 and 6.5 (Section 6.3 onward)

positivity for supp f in (1/2, 2); a numerical-analysis proof (per Connes 2026, Section 4.1)
history.note: Adv. Stud. Pure Math. 21 (1992) 281-325; read via Connes 2026, not opened

history.value: operator-theoretic (Sonin compression) reason for the same window; 13 < c < 17
for sufficiently small a the lowest eigenvalue lambda_a of the localized Weil operator is > 0, simple, with even eigenfunction (LED-OPS-11)

caveats: The window contains no prime, so this says nothing about prime contributions. Positivity for all windows [1/lambda, lambda] is equivalent to RH. The proof relies on computer calculations (Fact 6.1, with m = 1732 trigonometric approximants; Fact 6.5). The text I read does not say that interval or ball arithmetic was used, so the certification status is unverified. No erratum found (one web search). I found no rigorous proof of Weil positivity for any window with lambda^2 > 2. This was not exhaustively checked; Bombieri (2000-2003) studied the functional, and I did not verify his ranges.

quantity: Prolate wave operator on the whole line: self-adjoint extension whose negative spectrum (Sonin space) has the UV behaviour of the squared zeta zeros
statement: The prolate operator W_lambda psi = -d((lambda^2 - x^2) d psi) + (2 pi lambda x)^2 psi has a unique self-adjoint extension W_sa on L^2(R). W_sa commutes with Fourier transform and has discrete spectrum unbounded in both directions (Theorem 2.6). Eigenvectors for negative eigenvalues lie in the Sonin space (Corollary 3.2). Proposition 4.2 gives a semiclassical count: the number of negative eigenvalues with |xi| <= E^2 is 2 sigma(E, lambda), with sigma(E, lambda) ~ (E/2pi)(log(E/2pi) - 1) + log 4 - 2 log lambda + lambda^2 + o(1). For lambda = sqrt 2, a Darboux/Riccati Dirac square root sqrt2 D has discrete simple spectrum in R union iR, with N(E) ~ (E/2pi)(log(E/2pi) - 1) + O(1) (Theorem 6.1). Positive eigenvalues match the squared trivial zeros, chi(n) = (2n + 1/2)^2 + O(1).
value: N(E) ~ (E/2pi)(log(E/2pi) - 1) + O(1): matches only the smooth Riemann–von Mangoldt main term
location: Theorem 2.6; Corollary 3.2; Proposition 4.2 (p. 10, eq. (23)); Theorem 6.1 (eq. (32)); Section 7.2

I did not find a rigorous eigenvalue-counting argument, so the UV agreement is graded heuristic. The agreement is with the smooth term only: the operator contains no primes and cannot reproduce S(T) or individual zeros.

quantity: Reality theorem: a simple, even ground state of a distributional convolution quadratic form has a Fourier transform with only real zeros (Carathéodory–Fejér analogue)
statement: Theorem 1.2 (precise form Theorem 6.1): let D be a real distribution on [0, L] and D~ its even extension to [-L, L]. Suppose the quadratic form with Schwartz kernel D~(x - y) defines a lower-bounded self-adjoint operator on L^2([-L/2, L/2]) whose spectral minimum is a simple, isolated eigenvalue with even eigenfunction xi. Then every zero of the entire function xi^(z) is real. Theorem 5.6 is the finite-dimensional version: let Q be a real symmetric positive matrix of the divided-difference ('spectral action') form, with off-diagonal entries (b_n - b_m)/(n - m) and b_{-n} = -b_n, and a one-dimensional even kernel. Then the associated trigonometric polynomial has only real zeros. Proof outline: a C*-algebraic proof of the Carathéodory–Fejér corollary, then the matrix analogue, then Hurwitz' theorem. Applied to the semilocal Weil form QW_lambda, which uses only primes p <= lambda^2: whenever the lowest eigenvalue of the Galerkin truncation QW_lambda^N is simple with an iota-even eigenvector, the Mellin transform of the ground state has all its zeros on the critical line.
value: (simple + isolated + even ground state) => all zeros of xi^ real; holds for every finite-prime window
conditional_on: Hypotheses inside the theorem: the lowest eigenvalue is simple and isolated, with an even eigenvector
location: Theorem 1.2 (p. 2), Theorem 5.6 (Section 5), Theorem 6.1 (p. 13); Remark 4.3 (says the Theorem 1.2 wording is 'slightly unprecise')

history.value: a positive semidefinite Toeplitz matrix of corank 1 has a kernel polynomial with zeros on the unit circle

history.value: used in the 'Letter to Riemann' to prove that the approximating values lie exactly on the critical line (arXiv 2602.04022)

caveats: This converts RH into two statements: the ground state of QW_lambda is simple and even for all large lambda, and the normalized ground states converge in a norm that controls the Mellin transform on the strip. Neither is proved. Suzuki (2606.09096) notes that what CCM actually prove concerns the Rayleigh minimizer on finite-dimensional subspaces, not the ground state of QW^a on L^2 itself.

quantity: Zeta spectral triples: rank-one perturbations D_log^(lambda,N) of the scaling operator on [1/lambda, lambda], built from primes p <= lambda^2
statement: Theorem 1.1 (= Theorem 5.10): let eps_N be the smallest eigenvalue of QW_lambda^N, assumed simple, with eigenvector xi assumed even and normalized by delta_N(xi) = 1. (i) D_log^(lambda,N) = D_log - |D_log xi><delta_N| is self-adjoint on E_N' + E_N-perp, with the inner product from QW_lambda^N - eps_N. (ii) det_reg(D_log^(lambda,N) - z) = -i lambda^{-iz} xi^(z). (iii) xi^ is entire and all its zeros are real; they coincide with the spectrum of D_log^(lambda,N). Numerically (Section 6), for lambda^2 = 12, 13, 14 and N = 120 the first eigenvalue matches gamma_1 to within 3.41e-50, 2.44e-55 and 1.07e-60. Section 7: 'Establishing this convergence rigorously would amount to a proof of the Riemann Hypothesis.' Section 8 names two missing steps: (1) prove that the smallest eigenvalue of QW_lambda is simple with even eigenvector; (2) prove that the prolate-built vector k_lambda approximates xi_lambda well enough for its zeros to converge to the zeta zeros.
value: first zero to 2.44e-55 (lambda^2 = 13, N = 120); 50 zeros, accuracy decaying to about 1e-3
conditional_on: Simplicity and evenness of the lowest eigenvalue of the truncated Weil form (checked numerically per (lambda, N))
location: Theorem 1.1 (pp. 2-3), Theorem 3.6 (discrete spectrum of A_lambda), Theorem 5.10, numerical table in Section 6 (p. 26), Section 7 Outlook, Section 8 'The missing steps' (pp. 32-33)

history.value: lambda^2 <= 14, N = 120: first zero to about 1e-60 at best
primes <= 13, first 50 zeros, errors from 2.60179e-55 to about 1e-3 (arXiv 2602.04022, p. 24)
cutoffs c = 13..67 at N = 100: first-zero error from about 2e-55 down to about 1.5e-168; c = 100: gamma_1..gamma_10 to 307-329 digits (arXiv 2605.20224, unrefereed)
lambda^2 = 250, N = 4000: first zero to 1341 digits (LED-OPS-10)

caveats: The hypothesis 'simple + even' is verified only numerically at finite N. The reported first-zero error differs slightly between documents: 2.44e-55 (CCM table), '2.5e-55' (CCM text) and 2.60179e-55 (Connes Letter, p. 24). These are upper bounds from presumably different truncations, not a substantive dispute. Disputes: (a) Śliwiński (arXiv 2601.12133, unrefereed) claims a 'theorem' that the mean absolute error is at least 1/(4 ln lambda). Its proof equates the eigenvalue error with the Heisenberg spread sigma of a state ('clearly bounded below'), a step I judge unjustified, so treat that bound as unverified. (b) R. Andrews Jr., 'Convergence claims for the CCM construction: an empirical reassessment' (Zenodo 2026, not located; known only from Andrews–Connes–La Gatta 2026, p. 7) found that along lambda = N the error over the whole finite spectrum grows while the low-lying zeros improve. (c) B. W. de Andrade Silva (Zenodo 10.5281/zenodo.20650146, June 2026) argues that negative even-sector eigenvalues reported by Groskin at c = 100 are quadrature artifacts, and corrects his own earlier ratio (c = 53, N = 100: 12922 -> 2738).

quantity: Lowest eigenvalue eps_lambda(1) of the semilocal Weil quadratic form QW_lambda on L^2([1/lambda, lambda], d*u): upper bound by the prolate (Fuchs) ladder
statement: Upper bound (a theorem of Connes–Kastoris, following Kastoris): eps_lambda <= C delta_4(lambda) (log lambda)^3. More generally eps_lambda(j) <= C_j delta_{4j}(lambda) (log lambda)^3 in the even sector and delta_{4j+2}(lambda) in the odd sector, for j <= K and lambda >= lambda_0(K) (Theorem 3.2 'after [11]'). Here delta_n(lambda) = 1 - |chi_n(lambda)| are the minuscule eigenvalues of Slepian's uncertainty operator U_lambda = 2 - P_lambda - P^_lambda, with Fuchs asymptotics delta_n(lambda) ~ c_n lambda^{2n+1} e^{-4 pi lambda^2}. The mechanism is the arithmetic map E(f)(u) = u^{1/2} sum_n f(nu) applied to Gevrey-smoothed prolate functions. The lower-bound direction ('nothing on the Weil side is smaller than U_lambda allows', Hypothesis 3.4) is NOT a theorem.
value: eps_lambda(1) <= C delta_4(lambda)(log lambda)^3, with delta_4(lambda) ~ c_4 lambda^9 e^{-4 pi lambda^2}. Numerically eps_lambda(1)/(delta_4(lambda) log lambda) lies in [4.9, 8.8] for 5 <= lambda^2 <= 300
location: arXiv 2611.13129: eq. (4) (p. 5), Theorem 3.1, Theorem 3.2 (p. ~16), Hypothesis 3.4; Fact 4.1 and Table 2

history.value: discovery of minuscule eigenvalues of QW_lambda with prolate-like eigenvectors (numerical)

The ratio data suggest that the exponent 3 is not sharp ('far from' optimal, per p. ~20). The Connes–Kastoris paper itself was not available to me; I graded from the restatement.

quantity: Weil ground state at large window: precision of zeta-zero reproduction, certified zero count at fixed lambda, and conditional positivity of QW_lambda
statement: With lambda^2 = 250 (the 53 primes < 250) and N = 4000 (an even sector of dimension 4001, about 2900 decimal digits), all zeros of the Mellin transform of the ground state are real by Theorem 7.1 (= Connes–van Suijlekom Theorem 5.6). The first 1000 zeros of zeta are reproduced with > 500 correct decimals, the first with 1341 (|t_1 - gamma_1| = 1.38999579112714e-1342). All 2469 zeta zeros of height <= 3000 are reproduced one-for-one within 1e-12. A certified ball-arithmetic sign count shows that the finite transform has no other zero, real or complex, in that range (Remark 7.2). The error is proportional to eps_lambda^N(1), uniformly in j. At fixed lambda the agreement breaks down near t ~ 3100 (lambda^2 = 250), independently of N. Proposition 7.3 (Hurwitz): if the normalized ground states converge to tau = theta/theta(1) in the weighted L^1 norm on both u and u^{-1}, then RH follows, because M theta(s) = (1/4) xi(s + 1/2) (Theorem 2.4). Section 6 obtains rates O(lambda^{-2}) only under Hypothesis 3.4 AND QW_lambda >= 0. Theorem 8.14 gives conditional positivity of QW_lambda on an explicit finite-codimension complement under a quantitative hypothesis (H2') on the semilocal cutoff projections. Positivity is reduced to a two-sided Schur-complement estimate on finitely many modes at the edge of the Fuchs ladder plus the two pole directions.
value: lambda^2 = 250, N = 4000: gamma_1 to 1341 digits; first 1000 zeros > 500 digits; 2469 zeros to height 3000 (>= 12 digits); breakdown at t ~ 3100. eps_lambda(1) ~ 1e-1346 (lambda^2 = 250), ~ 1e-1618 (lambda^2 = 300). After conditioning, the form is bounded below by mu_lambda ~ 2/lambda (0.78 at lambda^2 = 5, 0.19 at lambda^2 = 150)
conditional_on: Section 6 rates: Hypothesis 3.4 (Fuchs-ladder lower bound) + QW_lambda >= 0. Theorem 8.14: hypothesis (H2')
location: Abstract; Introduction pp. 3-7; Theorem 7.1, Remark 7.2, Proposition 7.3, Remark 7.4 (pp. 31-32); Section 7.3 and table (51) (p. 33); Theorem 8.1, Theorem 8.14, Propositions 8.17-8.18
caveats: Remark 7.4 (the authors): the conditional convergence assumes QW_lambda >= 0, which for all lambda is equivalent to RH, so 'the conditional results therefore do not give a proof'. An unconditional treatment needs the lower-bound direction of Hypothesis 3.4. The certified sign count certifies the zeros of the finite transform at one (lambda, N). It does not certify positivity of QW_lambda: a positive Galerkin truncation is an upper section, not a lower certificate. The fixed-lambda breakdown shows that no single finite window suffices. The comparison with zeta zeros is high-precision numerics against reference ordinates; the reference gamma_1 was independently checked to 1400 digits. Groskin's reported negative eigenvalues at c = 100 are disputed as quadrature artifacts (de Andrade Silva, Zenodo 2026).

quantity: Localized Weil form operators A_a on L^2(-a, a) (log scale): unconditional structure, simplicity and evenness for small a, and self-adjoint differentiation operators with real simple spectrum
statement: Unconditionally: A_a is a lower-bounded self-adjoint operator (Theorem 1.1); its lowest eigenvalue lambda_a is continuous (Theorem 1.3) and non-increasing in a (Corollary 1.2). Theorem 1.4: for sufficiently small a > 0, lambda_a is positive and simple with even eigenfunction, and lambda_a = log(1/a) + mu_1 - log(2pi) + psi(2) - 1 + O(a) for some mu_1 > 0. Theorem 1.5: for any lambda < lambda_a, D_a = i d/dx on the completion H(T_a), T_a = A_a - lambda, has deficiency indices (1,1). For every theta, the zeros of the entire function W(a, theta; z) are exactly the eigenvalues of the self-adjoint extension D_{a,theta}, and they are real and simple. Corollary 1.6: if suitable normalizations make e^{phi(a,z)} W(a, theta; z) -> xi(1/2 - iz)/(xi(1/2 - iz) + xi'(1/2 - iz)) locally uniformly in the upper half-plane, then RH holds.

location: Theorems 1.1, 1.3, 1.4, 1.5 and Corollary 1.6 (pp. 5-7); Section 7 (heuristics for (1.12))

quantity: RH-conditional spectral convergence of localized Weil-form differentiation operators to the distinct zero ordinates
statement: Theorem 1.1: assume RH, and let 0 < t_{a,1} < t_{a,2} < ... be the positive eigenvalues of the self-adjoint extension D_{a,pi} of D_a on H(A_a). Then for every n >= 1, t_{a,n} >= gamma_n and t_{a,n} decreases monotonically to gamma_n as a -> infinity, where gamma_n are the distinct positive ordinates. Theorem 1.2: assume RH; then W(a, pi; z)/W(a, pi; 0) -> Delta_Gamma(z) = prod over distinct gamma > 0 of (1 - z^2/gamma^2), uniformly on compacta. Under RH + simple zeros, the limit is xi(1/2 - iz)/xi(1/2). The key step expresses the inverse of the local extension as a compression of the inverse of a global self-adjoint operator.

Sarnak gave a computation-free proof of the F(W) failure, using density of the values of log zeta in 1/2 < Re s < 2, and extended it to all Dirichlet L-functions. quantity: de Branges structure (Hermite–Biehler) functions built from xi: what is unconditional and where RH enters (Lagarias)
statement: Lagarias 2005 (Acta Arith.), Lemma 2.1/6.1 and Theorem 2.1: E_h(z) = xi(1/2 + h - iz) is a de Branges structure function (|E_h(z)| > |E_h(z-bar)| for Im z > 0) unconditionally for |h| >= 1/2, and for all h != 0 under RH. Consequently, for |h| >= 1/2 and every theta, A_{h,theta} and B_{h,theta} (e.g. (xi(s+h) +- xi(s-h))/2) have all zeros on Re s = 1/2, simple and interlacing. These zeros are the spectrum of self-adjoint extensions of multiplication by z in H(E_h), and their normalized spacings tend to 1 (GUE destroyed). The same holds for primitive Dirichlet characters. Lagarias 2006 (Frontiers I), per the zbMATH review: with A_chi(z) = xi_chi(1/2 - iz) and B_chi(z) = i xi_chi'(1/2 - iz), E_chi = A_chi - iB_chi is a de Branges function iff RH holds for L(s, chi), and a strict de Branges function iff RH holds and all zeros are simple.
value: h >= 1/2: unconditional; 0 < h < 1/2: <=> RH-type (implied by RH); h -> 0 / E_xi = xi + xi': <=> RH (+ simplicity)
conditional_on: RH needed for 0 < h < 1/2 (a partial unconditional extension by X. Li was not verified)

The RH gap is the passage h -> 0, equivalently Hermite–Biehler membership of xi + xi'. The approach needs a construction of the space or its Hamiltonian that does not presuppose this membership (see LED-OPS-15).

quantity: Explicit canonical systems (Hamiltonians) realizing xi-type de Branges functions (Suzuki, following Burnol)
statement: Suzuki 2012/2016, Theorem 2.3: for omega > 1, let H_{omega,a} = P_a H_omega P_a be the compressed Hankel-type operator. It is Hilbert–Schmidt and self-adjoint with continuous kernel, and 1 +- H_{omega,a} is invertible for all a > 0. With m(a) = det(1 + H_{omega,a})/det(1 - H_{omega,a}), the canonical system -a d/da (X_a, Y_a) = z J diag(m(a)^{-2}, m(a)^2)(X_a, Y_a) has an explicit solution with (A_1, B_1) = (A^omega, B^omega) = ((xi(s+omega) + xi(s-omega))/2, (i/2)(xi(s+omega) - xi(s-omega))), s = 1/2 - iz. There is an equivalent pair of Schrödinger equations with explicit potentials V^+-. The limit a -> infinity is left open. Suzuki 2020 (arXiv 1606.05726 v3), Theorem 2.4: for L in the class S_R (a subclass of the Selberg class), GRH(L) holds iff there is a sequence (omega_n, nu_n) with omega_n decreasing to 0, nu_n omega_n d_L > 1, det(1 +- K_L^{omega_n, nu_n}[t]) != 0 for all t >= 0, and lim_{t -> inf} J_L^{omega_n, nu_n}(t; z, z) = 0 on C_+. The Hamiltonian exists unconditionally on some [0, tau) (Theorem 2.1).
value: Hamiltonian explicit for omega > 1 (zeta); for all omega > 0 on [0, tau) for L in S_R. RH <=> extension to [0, infinity) plus the boundary condition at infinity

quantity: Scattering-theory formulations: Lax–Phillips and Faddeev–Pavlov (modular group) and Burnol's adelic causality
statement: For automorphic functions on SL_2(Z) the scattering matrix is a ratio of completed zeta values. Lax–Phillips: if RH were true, the poles of the scattering matrix would lie on the line Im sigma = 1/4 and the spectrum of the generator B'' of the Lax–Phillips semigroup Z''(t) on the line Re lambda = -1/4. A necessary condition is an exponential decay estimate for Z''(t) f on a dense set of f in K'' (the formula is illegible in the OCR). Faddeev–Pavlov (1972) found 'a similar condition which is both necessary and sufficient for the validity of the Riemann hypothesis'. Lax–Phillips' own assessment: the averaging over the group 'arithmetizes the problem and throws the exponential decay of Z''(t)f back onto number theoretical considerations', so 'we do not believe that this approach will be helpful in verifying the Riemann hypothesis'. Burnol (2001): to any global field K he attaches a Lax–Phillips scattering that is causal iff RH holds for all abelian L-functions of K (an adelic Nyman–Beurling-type closure problem).
value: RH <=> decay/causality statement (equivalence only; no partial unconditional decay rate toward RH known to me)
location: pp. XXIII.6-XXIII.7 (numdam SEDP_1973-1974____A21_0); Faddeev–Pavlov, Zap. Nauchn. Sem. LOMI 27 (1972) 161-193 (cited, not opened); Burnol, J. Number Theory 87 (2001) 253-269, arXiv math/0001013 (abstract)

quantity: Berry–Keating xp and Sierra regularizations: proven spectral content
statement: Rigorous: H_BK = -i hbar(x d/dx + 1/2) on L^2(R_>0) has purely continuous spectrum, so this quantization cannot be a Hilbert–Pólya operator. All self-adjoint realizations on compact quantum graphs are classified, with an exact trace formula and Weyl law (Endres–Steiner 2010). Srednicki (2011) gives a spectral proof of the archimedean 'local RH': the zeros of Mellin transforms of Hermite functions lie on Re = 1/2, as eigenvalues of xp projected onto lower oscillator levels. Semiclassical (heuristic): regularized xp phase-space areas reproduce the smooth count N_bar(E) = (E/2pi)(log(E/2pi) - 1) + 7/8 (Berry–Keating 1999); Connes 1999 eq. (43) gives it with a minus sign, as missing states. Sierra–Rodríguez-Laguna (2011): H = x(p + l_p^2/p) has closed orbits and a spectrum coinciding with the AVERAGE zeros. Hwang–Jung–Kim–Park (2026, unrefereed) compare 606 eigenvalues of the SRL-type extension (theta = 1.417 pi) with gamma_n and find E_n - gamma_n ~ (theta - pi/4)/[1 + W(n/e)], which decays only like 1/ln n. They fit a coefficient of 3.666 against Odlyzko's first 1e5 zeros, and the scatter is the S(T) term. Sierra (2019) gives a 'local' Hilbert–Pólya realization: a zero E_n is a bound state of H_theta only if theta is fine-tuned to theta(E_n) + (pi/2) sign Z'(E_n). His RH argument 'assumes the convergence of some mathematical series'.
value: only the smooth term N_bar(E) is reproduced; discrepancies E_n - gamma_n of order 1/ln n (SRL type); no model reproduces S(T) without inserting zeta/primes

quantity: Bender–Brody–Müller pseudo-Hermitian Hamiltonian and its critique
statement: BBM: H = Delta^{-1}(xp + px)Delta-type, with Delta f(x) = f(x) - f(x-1). With the boundary condition psi_z(0) = 0, the eigenvalues correspond to the nontrivial zeros. H is not Hermitian; iH is PT-symmetric with broken PT symmetry. The metric operator is constructed 'heuristically', and the authors write: 'If the analysis presented here can be made rigorous to show that H is manifestly self-adjoint, then this implies that the Riemann hypothesis holds true.' Bellissard's comment: (1) on L^2(0, inf), p with the Dirichlet condition f(0) = 0 is symmetric, but its adjoint has every point of the upper half-plane as an eigenvalue. Its deficiency indices are (n+, n-) = (1, 0), so it has NO self-adjoint extension, and the argument 'cannot be used'. (2) The eigenfunction psi_z is in L^2 near 0 only for Re z > 3/2, so it is not an eigenvector for Re z = 1/2. Weighted spaces x^alpha dx shift the dilation generator by i(alpha + 1)/2 and lose the critical line. BBM's reply (arXiv 1705.06767) states that the issues 'have already been discussed in the paper and do not affect the conclusions'.
value: no proven spectral statement; the momentum operator has deficiency indices (1, 0), so no self-adjoint extension exists
location: BBM abstract and p. 2; Bellissard pp. 1-3 ('Problem 1', 'Problem 2', Conclusion)
