verification.checked_against: TTY Lemma 29 p. 16, eq. (27) A(1/2) = 2, Lemma 40 p. 25 (MT24 = 2403.13157), Heuristic 54 discussion; GM footnote 1 and pp. 3–4; Guth 2503.07410 §3.4 (Conj. 3.3/3.4), §3.5, §4 ('not able to check … even for N = 200'), §6, §8 (Mao–Wein), §9 pp. 39–40
verification.correction: (iv) Bourgain showed that Montgomery's ℓ^q conjecture (Guth Conj. 3.4) implies the Bourgain–Kakeya conjecture 9.3, which implies Kakeya (Conj. 9.1) in every dimension. DH itself is not known to imply Kakeya, so the barrier applies only to proving DH through the full Conj. 3.4 for all 1-bounded polynomials. (vi) Mao–Wein's failure of low-degree tests is a theorem. Only the step to 'no polynomial-time algorithm' depends on the low-degree conjecture. A barrier specific to the 30/13 bottleneck is missing and should be added. GM §13.1 Remark says that at the critical configuration (σ = 7/10, length T^{10/13}, subintervals T₁ = T^{12/13}, |W| ≈ T₁^{2/3}, E(W) ≈ |W|^{5/2} ≈ |W|^4/T₁) the S1 and S2 bounds are best possible, any gain must come from S3, the E(W) bound sits at the random-set level, and the §9 argument is essentially tight there.

quantity: Uniform zero-free half-plane, human-edited companion argument (exponent 11/12)
statement: Theorem 1.1 (OpenAI, 5 Oct 2026): every finite-order Hecke L-function over K = Q(sqrt(-3)) has no zeros in Re s > 11/12. Hence every Dirichlet L-function, including zeta(s), has no zeros for Re s > 11/12. The proof reduces to Proposition 3.1. Let A_u(D) = sum over n coprime to S of mu(n) nu(n) chi_n(u) W(N(n)/D), with sextic residue symbols chi_n(u) = (u/n)_6. For 0 < theta <= 1/10, Proposition 3.1 claims sum_{0<N(u)<=D^{1+theta}} |A_u(D)|^2 << D^{2+theta+eps}. Taking the rows u = p^6 with N(p) about Y = H^{1/6} gives |A_1(D)|^2 << D^{11/6+5theta/6+eps} + D^{5/3-theta/3}, so A_1(D) << D^{11/12+eps}. A Mellin argument then excludes zeros. Corollary 1.2: sup_{q<=x} |pi(x;q,a) - li(x)/phi(q)| << x^{11/12} log x, with an absolute, effective constant.
value: B = 11/12 (claimed; not refereed)
conditional_on: Correctness of Proposition 3.1, the mean-square estimate. This is the smallest statement whose failure would invalidate the 11/12 claim.
location: Theorem 1.1 pp.1-2; Corollary 1.2 p.2; outline Section 2 pp.3-5, eqs. (2.1)-(2.5); Proposition 3.1 and the full deduction of Theorem 1.1 from it, p.11, eq. (3.2)-(3.3)

history.note: Isolated as a 'natural intermediate step' toward 7/8. Per the OpenAI repository README, it is the only write-up in the release edited by a human.

caveats: I read Section 3 (Prop 3.1 implies Theorem 1.1, one page). It is elementary given Prop 3.1. Prop 3.1 itself (Sections 4-7 and the appendices) was NOT audited. That proof uses Poisson summation in u, Gauss-Jacobi identities turning sextic Gauss sums into cubic ones, automorphy of Kubota's cubic theta function, Dunn-Radziwill cusp expansions, and a recursive character large sieve. Per Quanta (secondary), there is no Lean formalization of this version. Specialists quoted largely judge it correct, but it is not refereed. Independent informal write-ups (7-13 pp.) reportedly circulate privately. PDF sha256 f919b57829b178c8e60e7c17b018cf773e7907cf642ef5a3347d8a826e8dbf18.

quantity: Classical (de la Vallee Poussin) constant R: zeta(sigma+it) != 0 for sigma > 1 - 1/(R log t), all t >= t0. Best claimed value
statement: Theorem 1 (Bellotti-Trudgian-Yang 2026): if t >= 3, then zeta(sigma+it) != 0 for sigma > 1 - 1/(4.896 log t). By conjugate symmetry the same holds for |t| >= 3. Lemma 1 proves the bound directly for 3 <= t <= exp(76.47). For t > exp(76.463) it follows from Yang's explicit Littlewood region (ZFR-07), which is wider there. The method combines Stechkin's pairing of rho with 1-rho and a new Heath-Brown-type smoothing weight f(u) = eta w(eta u) h(u). It uses a degree-16 nonnegative trigonometric polynomial and RH verified to H = 3*10^12.
conditional_on: Correctness of Yang 2024 (refereed) and of the RH verification to 3*10^12 (Platt-Trudgian 2021).
location: Theorem 1 and Lemma 1, p.2; deduction p.2 using eqs. (3)-(4); trigonometric polynomial and Lemma 10 pp.15-16; Table 1 (certified m_p) p.17
caveats: Unrefereed preprint, but a complete proof by established specialists. Improvement over 5.558691 is 11.9% in R, i.e. a 13.5% wider region. The proof is computer-assisted. The bound d G_p/d sigma < 0 for primes p < 100 was 'verified numerically, using Mathematica', which is not stated as interval or certified arithmetic. Only the polynomial minima m_p are certified by exact real-algebraic verification. The certification gate is therefore partial. There is a minor internal inconsistency: Lemma 1 is stated for 3 <= t, while the deduction text says 2 <= t. The theorem depends on Yang's Littlewood region (ZFR-07) beyond exp(76.463).

Their constants are far larger than the roughly k^{O(k^4)} size that Ford's argument can absorb. MTY note that Preobrazhenskii's improvement should give a slight reduction in B.

quantity: Ford's 2002 explicit regions and their published corrections (intermediate-t classical-type region; classical R = 8.463)
statement: Ford arXiv:1910.08205v5 (18 Feb 2025) is the corrected version of the 2002 paper. Its comment reads: 'corrected typos in Lemma 2.2, numerics in (8.8) and (8.9), and fixed the argument following Lemma 9.2. Compared to the published version, Theorems 1 and 5 are unchanged, Theorem 4 is very slightly degraded, and Theorems 2 and 3 have different numerics.' In v5, Theorem 4 is zeta(beta+it) != 0 for |t| >= 3 and 1 - beta <= 1/(8.464 log|t|); the published value was 8.463. Theorem 3 (t >= T0 = 5.45*10^8) gives 1 - beta <= (0.04962 - c6(t))/(J(t) + 0.155 log log t + 0.675), with J(t) = min(1/4 log t + 1.8521, 1/6 log t + log log t + log 3). Footnote 1 says Lemma 3 of Cheng-Graham, which is behind their bound |zeta(1/2+it)| <= 3 t^{1/6} log t, contains an unfixable error. Claimed improvements by Trudgian and by Hiary also used that lemma. The repair is Hiary-Patel-Yang: |zeta(1/2+it)| <= 0.618 |t|^{1/6} log|t| for |t| >= 3.
value: R = 8.464 (corrected; published 8.463); VK 57.54 unchanged
location: Theorems 1-5, pp.1-3; footnote 1, p.3; arXiv v5 comment
caveats: ERRATUM-PROPAGATION RISK. MTY (eq. 1.8, citing v4 of Sept 2022) and Yang (eq. 1.4, citing the published Theorem 3) both quote Ford's Theorem 3 in the form (0.04962 - 0.0196/(J+1.15))/(J + 0.685 + 0.155 log log t). Both use it to claim the widest region for roughly exp(46-64) to exp(170). v5 states a different form of Theorem 3 (with c6(t) and +0.675). I did not check whether the v5 numerics reproduce the region quoted by MTY and Yang. Their intermediate-range optimality claims should be re-checked against v5. The Cheng-Graham error affects any explicit region that relied on the 3 t^{1/6} log t midline bound.

verification.checked_against: arXiv:1910.08205v5 (18 Feb 2025): the arXiv comment, Theorems 1-5, eqs. (1.6)-(1.8), footnote 1, and the definitions of c6, c7 and L2 (Section 9). arXiv v1 (Theorem 3 in its published form). MTY eq. (1.8) and reference [10] (v4, 22 Sep 2022). Yang eq. (1.4).
verification.notes: The quotes are accurate. I also numerically compared v5 Theorem 3 against the published form. Published: (0.04962 - 0.0196/(J+1.15))/(J+0.685+0.155 log log t). v5: (0.04962 - c6(t))/(J+0.155 log log t+0.675), with c6 = 0.05635[J(4t+1) - J(t) + 0.155(L2 - log log t)]/(J + 0.155 log log t + 0.675). For log t >= 30 the v5 width is at least as large as the published one, both with log 3 and with the HPY log 0.618 substitution. Examples at log t = 64.1: 2.8261e-3 vs 2.8064e-3 (log 3), and 3.1055e-3 vs 3.0815e-3 (HPY). So MTY's and Yang's intermediate-range claims, which use the published form, are not weakened by the correction, which can only widen those regions slightly. This resolves the ledger's open question, modulo the validity of substituting HPY into Ford's method. Ford v5 still states (1.6) as Cheng-Graham's bound. Its validity rests on footnote 1's replacements (Lehman 4(t/2pi)^{1/4} and HPY 0.618 t^{1/6} log t), both of which are stronger than the bounds actually used, so Theorems 3-5 survive.

quantity: Intermediate explicit region from midline sub-Weyl bounds (MTY Theorem 1.4)
statement: Theorem 1.4 (MTY): there are no zeros of zeta(sigma+it) for |t| >= exp(1000) and sigma > 1 - 0.05035/h(t) + 0.0349/h^2(t), where h(t) = (27/164) log|t| + 7.096. It uses Patel's sub-Weyl bound |zeta(1/2+it)| <= 307.098 |t|^{27/164}. MTY's 2022 summary of the widest region by height: RH up to 3*10^12; classical 5.558691 up to exp(64.1); Ford (1.8) up to exp(1000); Theorem 1.4 up to exp(52238); VK 55.241 beyond. Yang 2024 and BTY 2026 later superseded parts of this envelope.

Current best envelope (combining refereed and preprint results): RH for |t| <= 3*10^12; BTY 4.896 up to about exp(76.46); possibly a Ford-type region up to about exp(170), pending ZFR-11; Yang 21.233 up to exp(482036); Bellotti 53.989 beyond.

quantity: Small-t regime: zero-free region near s = 1 for bounded height
statement: All non-trivial zeros with 0 < |gamma| <= 3*10^12 lie on Re s = 1/2. So for |t| <= 3*10^12, zeta(sigma+it) != 0 for sigma > 1/2. Every explicit classical, Littlewood or VK region above is used only beyond this height; e.g. BTY eq. (5) sets H = 3*10^12. There are no non-trivial zeros with |t| < 14.13.
value: zero-free for sigma > 1/2 when |t| <= 3*10^12
location: Main theorem (cited as [12] in BTY 2026 eq. (5), p.3 and as [24] in MTY p.3)
caveats: Primary paper not opened here. Accepted as a rigorous interval-arithmetic computation by the cited explicit literature. Higher non-rigorous verifications exist, but they are not certified and must not be used as inputs.

quantity: Dirichlet L-functions: classical explicit constant R in sigma >= 1 - 1/(R log(q max(1,|t|)))
statement: McCurley (1984): L(sigma+it,chi) != 0 for t >= 0 and sigma >= 1 - 1/(9.64590880 log max{q, qt, 10}), apart from a possible simple real (Landau-Siegel) zero. This is quoted as eq. (2.3) in Khale. Kadiri (2018): for every non-principal primitive chi mod q with 3 <= q <= 400000, L(s,chi) has no zeros in Re s >= 1 - 1/(R log(q max(1,|Im s|))) with R = 5.60. Her 2001 thesis had R = 6.436.
value: R = 9.645908801 (all q, one possible exceptional zero); R = 5.60 (3 <= q <= 400000)
location: McCurley Theorem 1.1 (via Khale arXiv:2210.06457, eq. (2.3), p.4); Kadiri main theorem (abstract and zbMATH Zbl 1412.11096 review)
caveats: Kadiri's range restriction matters, and no comparable general-q improvement over McCurley was verified here. The claimed quasi-RH results (ZFR-01 to ZFR-03), if correct, would exclude Landau-Siegel zeros and make every one of these regions obsolete. They remain unrefereed.

quantity: Dirichlet L-functions: explicit Vinogradov-Korobov region
statement: Theorem 1.1 (Khale): for q >= 3 and any Dirichlet character chi mod q, L(sigma+it,chi) != 0 for sigma >= 1 - 1/(10.5 log q + 61.5 (log|t|)^{2/3}(log log|t|)^{1/3}), |t| >= 10. There is an effectively computable Y such that the region with 10.1 log q + 49.13 (log|t|)^{2/3}(log log|t|)^{1/3} holds for |t| >= Y. The proof uses Ford's A = 76.2, B = 4.45 and McCurley's classical region below t = e^{1944}.

history.value: first explicit VK region for Dirichlet L-functions

caveats: Footnote: the results depend on Ford's calculations, and Ford later issued corrections (v5, ZFR-11). Theorems 1 and 5 are unchanged, so the 49.13 asymptotic is presumably unaffected, but this was not re-checked. MTY note that higher-degree trigonometric polynomials and Bellotti's B would improve the constants. Khale remarks that an unpublished result would lower 61.306 to 59.521.

quantity: Negative result: optimality of the classical region (and of any wider contour) under Beurling hypotheses
statement: Diamond-Montgomery-Vorhauer (Math. Ann. 334, 2006) construct Beurling generalized prime systems whose integers satisfy N(x) = Ax + O(x^theta) with theta >= 1/2, yet whose zeta functions have zeros on a de la Vallee Poussin contour. Hence the classical region cannot be improved using only the Euler product plus integer-count regularity. Broucke (2025, Theorem 1.6) generalizes this. Let f be eventually C^1, decreasing and strictly convex, with 1/u = o(f(u)), and either regularly varying of index -alpha (0 < alpha <= 1) or slowly varying with (1.10). Then there is a Beurling system with N_P(x) = Ax + O_eps(x^{1/2+eps}) whose zeta has infinitely many zeros on sigma = 1 - f(log|t|) and none to the right. It also has a matching Omega_plus-minus PNT error term. Broucke-Revesz (arXiv:2611.03356) further show zeros near the 1-line must occur in clusters.
value: qualitative: any contour from Littlewood/VK shape (alpha = 1 or 2/3) to slowly varying shapes such as 1/log u is attainable by Beurling zetas
location: Theorem 1.6 and the paragraph following, p.6; reference [8]

history.value: classical region sharp under Beurling Axiom A
generalization to all convex contours of index -alpha, and slowly varying ones

caveats: This is a barrier to methods, not a statement about zeta. Wider regions for zeta must use arithmetic beyond Euler product plus N(x) = Ax + O(x^{1/2+eps}). VK uses the exponential-sum structure of n^{-it}. The claimed quasi-RH proofs use cubic/sextic residue symbols and metaplectic theta functions over Q(sqrt(-3)). The Broucke paper is an arXiv preprint; DMV is refereed.

source.authors: F. Broucke (building on H. G. Diamond, H. L. Montgomery, U. M. A. Vorhauer)
source.title: On the connection between zero-free regions and the error term in the Prime Number Theorem

verification.checked_against: arXiv:2507.13780v1, Theorem 1.6 and the paragraph after it (p.6), and reference [8] (DMV, Math. Ann. 334 (2006), 1-36). The arXiv abstract of 2611.03356 (Broucke and Revesz, 'On Landau's local method for obtaining zero-free regions', 2 Nov 2026).
verification.notes: Transcribed correctly. One framing point: Theorem 1.6 assumes 1/u = o(f(u)), i.e. contours further from the 1-line than de la Vallee Poussin's. Its role in the paper is to show that the transfer from zero-free region to PNT error (Theorem 1.5) is essentially sharp. The barrier 'Euler product plus N(x) = Ax + O(x^theta) gives nothing beyond dlVP' is DMV's theorem; Broucke's result adds that every wider convex contour is also attainable. I did not open DMV directly.

quantity: Negative/limit results for the trigonometric-polynomial and smoothing (zero-detector) method of the classical constant
statement: Landau's V = lim_n inf_{f in P_n} (f(0) - a0)/(sqrt(a1) - sqrt(a0))^2 controls the classical constant in the Landau/Stechkin method: R0 = V/2 + eps (Landau), R0 = (V/2)(1 - 1/sqrt5) + eps (Stechkin). Mossinghoff-Trudgian Theorem 2: 34.468305 < V < 34.4889920009. The lower bound is due to Arestov-Kondrat'ev 1990, so these methods cannot go below about 9.5. Smoothing (Heath-Brown 1992; Kadiri 2005) circumvents this barrier. BTY 2026 measure the efficiency c of the zero-detector weight: c = 1 for Heath-Brown's, 1.78 for Kadiri's, 1.98 for their discrete approximation, and c = 2 for the hypothetical optimal weight h(u) = 1/(1 + e^{-(2 sigma - 1)u}). They call their weight 'within one percent of the hypothetical limit of the method'.
value: 34.468305 < V < 34.4889920009; BTY efficiency 1.98 of a hypothetical maximum 2
location: MT 2015: eqs. (1.1)-(1.3), Theorem 2, p.3. BTY: Section 2, p.6, discussion after eq. (20).

history.value: optimal Landau polynomials of degrees 7 and 8 (numerical)

caveats: The 'efficiency' limit in BTY is a heuristic within their framework, not a theorem that R cannot go below a given value. Leong-Mossinghoff (arXiv:2404.05928) show 3 + 4cos + cos2 is optimal for Titchmarsh's lower bound of |zeta(sigma+it)| with sigma > 1, a related but distinct extremal problem.

(13)-(20) and the efficiency remark. arXiv metadata of 2411.01385v2 (Hong Sheng Tan, degrees 7 and 8) and 2404.05928v3 (Leong-Mossinghoff).

quantity: Equivalence-type link between the zero-free region and the PNT error term (why the region matters)
statement: Pintz (1980): a zero-free region of VK type with constant c gives pi(x) - li(x) << x exp(-d (log x)^{3/5} (log log x)^{-1/5}), with d = (5^6/(2^2 3^4 c^2))^{1/5}, and conversely the error term determines the region. MTY: c = 48.1588 gives d >= 0.2123. Bellotti (arXiv:2508.02041) shows N(sigma,T) is bounded by an absolute constant near the left edge of the VK region. It then claims the optimal form psi(x) - x << x exp(-omega(x)) with omega(x) = min_t {nu(t) log x + log t}, i.e. epsilon = 0 in the Pintz-Johnston formulation.
value: d >= 0.2123 (with c = 48.1588); slightly larger with Bellotti's 48.0718
location: MTY Section 2, p.4. Bellotti 2508.02041 (abstract only).

history.value: zero-free region equivalent to PNT error
refined error with (log x)^9/(log log x)^3 factor

caveats: Bellotti 2025 and Johnston are not fully read here (abstracts only). The formula for d is quoted from MTY.
